akhfash:3-3.t: [He said] ﴿هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِّلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ (accusative) because His word ﴿الۤـمۤ [1] تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾ [2] is definite, and this is a khabar (predicate) for the definite. «[Translator's note: i.e. it is accusative as a ḥāl coming after a complete definite statement.]»

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said ﴿أَنِ ٱشْكُرْ للَّهِ﴾: it is "that is: be grateful to Allah" (بِأَنِ اشْكُرِ اللهَ).

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿وَفِصَالُهُ فِي عَامَيْنِ﴾, i.e. at the end of two years; He did not mention "the end", just as He said ﴿وَسْئَلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning the people of the town.

akhfash:16-16.t:
And He said ﴿إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ﴾ (if it should) amount to, i.e. "if a sin should be the weight of a grain". Some put it in the nominative and made it the "كانَ" that does not need a khabar (predicate), as though it were "if the weight of a grain should come to be".
And He said ﴿إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾: He means "if the act of disobedience should be the weight of a mustard seed".

akhfash:21-21.t: And He said ﴿أَوَلَوْ كَانَ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ يَدْعُوهُمْ﴾: here is the interrogative alif, which he put before the wāw of conjunction.

akhfash:27-27.t: And He said ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلاَمٌ وَٱلْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ﴾: (البحر is) nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and accusative by qaṭʿ (severance). And "the pens" are nominative as the khabar (predicate) of "أَنَّ".

akhfash:34-34.t: And He said ﴿وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾: you may say "أَيُّ امْرَأَةٍ جاءَتْكَ" and "أَيَّةُ امْرَأَةٍ جاءَتْكَ" (which woman came to you?).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الم﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ i.e. these verses ﴿آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Qurʾān ﴿الْحَكِيمِ﴾ possessed of wisdom; the annexation (iḍāfa) is in the sense of مِنْ. It is

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿هُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾ in the nominative ﴿لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾; and in the reading of the generality [of readers] [هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً] in the accusative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الآيات, its governing word (ʿāmil) being the sense of pointing contained in تِلْكَ.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَوةَ﴾ an explanation (bayān) of الْمُحْسِنِينَ, ﴿وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَوةَ وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ the second هُمْ is tawkīd (emphasis).

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَلَى هُدًى مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ the triumphant.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ﴾ i.e. such of it as distracts from what matters, ﴿لِيَضِلَّ﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with ḍamma [لِيُضِلَّ] ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ the way of Islam ﴿بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّخِذَهَا﴾ in the accusative, conjoined to يُضِلَّ, and in the nominative, conjoined to يَشْتَرِي, ﴿هُزُوًا﴾ an object of mockery; ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ﴾ involving humiliation.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا﴾ i.e. the Qurʾān, ﴿وَلَّى مُسْتَكْبِرًا﴾ arrogant, ﴿كَأَنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْهَا كَأَنَّ فِي أُذُنَيْهِ وَقْرًا﴾ deafness — the two clauses of comparison are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun of وَلَّى, or the second is an explanation (bayān) of the first — ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُ﴾ inform him ﴿بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ painful; the mention of «glad tidings» is mockery of him. He is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith: he used to go to al-Ḥīra to trade, and would buy books of the stories of the Persians and relate them to the people of Mecca, saying: Muḥammad tells you the stories of ʿĀd and Thamūd, and I tell you the stories of Persia and Byzantium. They found his talk pleasing and abandoned listening to the Qurʾān.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. their abiding in it being destined when they enter it; ﴿وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا﴾ i.e. Allah has promised them that, and made it true, truly; ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ whom nothing overcomes so as to prevent Him from fulfilling His promise and His threat, ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ who puts nothing anywhere but in its proper place.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا﴾ i.e. the pillars — ʿamad is the plural of ʿimād, which is a column — and this holds true if there are no pillars at all; ﴿وَأَلْقَى فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ﴾ lofty mountains, so ﴿أَنْ﴾ [it may] not ﴿تَمِيدَ﴾ shake ﴿بِكُمْ وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَأَنْزَلْنَا﴾ in it is iltifāt (a shift of person) away from the third person, ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ fine kind.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿هَذَا خَلْقُ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. what He has created; ﴿فَأَرُونِي﴾ tell me, O people of Mecca, ﴿مَاذَا خَلَقَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ other than Him, i.e. your gods, such that you associate them with Him, exalted is He. مَا is an interrogative of disapproving denial and a mubtadaʾ (subject); ذَا, in the sense of «that which» (alladhī), with its ṣila (relative clause), is its khabar (predicate); أَرُونِي is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing, and what follows it stands in place of the two objects. ﴿بَلِ﴾ for transition: ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear, through their associating partners, and you are among them.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا لُقْمَانَ الْحِكْمَةَ﴾ including knowledge, religiousness and correctness in speech; his wise sayings are many and handed down. He used to give legal opinions before the mission of David, lived to see his mission, took knowledge from him and gave up giving legal opinions; he said about that: shall I not be content when I have been spared [the need]? And he was asked: which of people is worst? He said: the one who does not care if people see him doing evil. ﴿أَنِ﴾ i.e. and We said to him: ﴿اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ﴾ for the wisdom He has given you; ﴿وَمَنْ يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ because the reward of his thanks is his; ﴿وَمَنْ كَفَرَ﴾ the blessing, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ﴾ independent of His creation, ﴿حَمِيدٌ﴾ praised in His making.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَ﴾ mention ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ يَا بُنَيَّ﴾ a diminutive of tenderness, ﴿لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ﴾ with Allah ﴿لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ — so he turned back to him and submitted to Islam.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ﴾ We commanded him to be dutiful to them; ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ﴾ and she weakened ﴿وَهْنًا عَلَى وَهْنٍ﴾ i.e. she grew weak from the pregnancy, weak from the labour pains and weak from the birth, ﴿وَفِصَالُهُ﴾ i.e. his weaning, ﴿فِي عَامَيْنِ﴾ and We said to him: ﴿أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيْكَ إِلَيَّ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ i.e. the return.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَإِنْ جَاهَدَاكَ عَلَى أَنْ تُشْرِكَ بِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾ in accordance with reality, ﴿فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِي الدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ i.e. with what is right — kindness and maintaining ties — ﴿وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ﴾ the way ﴿مَنْ أَنَابَ﴾ has turned back ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ in obedience; ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and I will requite you for it. The clause of the injunction and what follows it is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ).

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿يَا بُنَيَّ إِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. the evil deed, ﴿إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ فَتَكُنْ فِي صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ أَوْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ i.e. in the most hidden place of that, ﴿يَأْتِ بِهَا اللَّهُ﴾ and He will call to account for it; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ﴾ in bringing it out, ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾ of its place.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿يَا بُنَيَّ أَقِمِ الصَّلَوةَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا أَصَابَكَ﴾ because of commanding and forbidding; ﴿إِنَّ ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ﴾ i.e. of the matters resolved upon, which one resolves upon because they are obligatory.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَلَا تُصَعِّرْ﴾ — in one reading [تُصَاعِرْ] — ﴿خَدَّكَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ do not turn your face away from them out of arrogance, ﴿وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا﴾ i.e. conceitedly; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتَالٍ﴾ strutting in his walk, ﴿فَخُورٍ﴾ over people.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ﴾ be moderate in it, between creeping and hurrying, and keep to calm and dignity; ﴿وَاغْضُضْ﴾ lower ﴿مِنْ صَوْتِكَ إِنَّ أَنْكَرَ الْأَصْوَاتِ﴾ the ugliest of them ﴿لَصَوْتُ الْحَمِيرِ﴾ its beginning is a braying out and its end a braying in.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَوْا﴾ know, O you addressed, ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُمْ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ the sun, the moon and the stars, that you may benefit from them, ﴿وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ fruits, rivers and beasts, ﴿وَأَسْبَغَ﴾ has made ample and complete ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظَاهِرَةً﴾ which is beauty of form, the proportioning of the limbs and so on, ﴿وَبَاطِنَةً﴾ it is knowledge [of Allah] and other things? ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿مَنْ يُجَادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلَا هُدًى﴾ from a messenger ﴿وَلَا كِتَابٍ مُنِيرٍ﴾ sent down by Allah, but rather out of blind imitation (taqlīd).

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا﴾. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿أَ﴾ would they follow it ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ يَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى عَذَابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾ i.e. to what brings it about? No.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. devotes himself to His obedience, ﴿وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ﴾ affirming His oneness, ﴿فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَى﴾ the firmest end, which there is no fear of breaking; ﴿وَإِلَى اللَّهِ عَاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ﴾ their return.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَلَا يَحْزُنْكَ﴾ O Muḥammad, ﴿كُفْرُهُ﴾ do not be concerned with his unbelief; ﴿إِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ فَنُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا عَمِلُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ﴾ i.e. of what is in them, as of other things, and so He will requite it.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿نُمَتِّعُهُمْ﴾ in this world ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ the days of their life, ﴿ثُمَّ نَضْطَرُّهُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿إِلَى عَذَابٍ غَلِيظٍ﴾ which is the punishment of the Fire; they will find no escape from it.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the lām of oath ﴿سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ﴾ — the nūn of the indicative (nūn al-rafʿ) has been dropped from it because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw of the pronoun because of the meeting of two quiescent letters — ﴿قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ for the manifestation of the proof against them for the oneness of Allah; ﴿بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is obligatory upon them.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ as possession, creation and servants, so none but He deserves worship in them; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ﴾ independent of His creation, ﴿الْحَمِيدُ﴾ the one praised in His making.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلَامٌ وَالْبَحْرُ﴾ conjoined to the noun (ism) of أَنَّ [وَالْبَحْرَ] ﴿يَمُدُّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍ﴾ as ink, ﴿مَا نَفِدَتْ كَلِمَاتُ اللَّهِ﴾ by which what He knows is expressed — by writing them with those pens and that ink, nor with more than that, because what He knows, exalted is He, is without limit; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾ nothing is beyond His power, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ nothing goes outside His knowledge and His wisdom.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿مَا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلَا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾ in creating and resurrecting, because it is by the word «Be», and it is; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ hears everything that can be heard, ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ sees everything that can be seen; nothing distracts Him from anything.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ know, O you addressed, ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُولِجُ﴾ makes enter ﴿اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهَارَ﴾ makes it enter ﴿فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ so each of them increases by what is decreased from the other, ﴿وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ﴾ of them ﴿يَجْرِي﴾ in its orbit ﴿إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾ which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾?

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned is ﴿بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ﴾ the firmly established, ﴿وَأَنَّ مَا يَدْعُونَ﴾ read with yāʾ and with tāʾ: they worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ الْبَاطِلُ﴾ the vanishing, ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ﴾ over His creation by subjugation, ﴿الْكَبِيرُ﴾ the mighty.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ الْفُلْكَ﴾ the ships ﴿تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِنِعْمَتِ اللَّهِ لِيُرِيَكُمْ﴾ O you addressed, by that, ﴿مِنْ آيَاتِهِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ﴾ lessons ﴿لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ﴾ in refraining from acts of disobedience to Allah, ﴿شَكُورٍ﴾ for His blessing.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَإِذَا غَشِيَهُمْ﴾ i.e. rose over the unbelievers ﴿مَوْجٌ كَالظُّلَلِ﴾ like mountains that overshadow whoever is beneath them, ﴿دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ i.e. the supplication that He save them, i.e. they do not call on anyone else with Him; ﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ فَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ﴾ midway between unbelief and faith, and among them is one who remains in his unbelief; ﴿وَمَا يَجْحَدُ بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ — among them the rescue from the waves — ﴿إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارٍ﴾ treacherous one, ﴿كَفُورٍ﴾ ungrateful for the blessings of Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. people of Mecca, ﴿اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَاخْشَوْا يَوْمًا لَا يَجْزِي﴾ avail ﴿وَالِدٌ عَنْ وَلَدِهِ﴾ in it anything, ﴿وَلَا مَوْلُودٌ هُوَ جَازٍ عَنْ وَالِدِهِ﴾ in it ﴿شَيْئًا إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ﴾ of the Resurrection, ﴿فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ away from Islam, ﴿وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ﴾ in His forbearance and His granting respite ﴿الْغَرُورُ﴾ the devil.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ﴾ when it will come; ﴿وَيُنْزِلُ﴾ read without and with doubling [وَيُنَزِّلُ] ﴿الْغَيْثَ﴾ at a time He knows, ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْأَرْحَامِ﴾ whether male or female — and none but Allah the Exalted knows any one of these three; ﴿وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ مَاذَا تَكْسِبُ غَدًا﴾ of good or evil, and Allah the Exalted knows it; ﴿وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾ and Allah the Exalted knows it; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of everything, ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾ of its inward as of its outward. Al-Bukhārī narrated from Ibn ʿUmar the hadith: "The keys of the unseen are five: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ to the end of the sūra."

daas-irab:1-2.t: ﴿الم﴾ Letters with no grammatical position. ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa) and has no grammatical position. ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْحَكِيمِ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of الكتاب.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿عَمَدٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَرَوْنَها﴾ An imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of عمد. ﴿وَأَلْقى﴾ Conjoined to خلق. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿رَواسِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْ تَمِيدَ﴾ An imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿وَبَثَّ﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِيها﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb as well. ﴿دابَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ماءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَنْبَتْنا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِيها﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb as well. ﴿زَوْجٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كَرِيمٍ﴾ An adjective of زوج; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿هذا خَلْقُ اللَّهِ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَأَرُونِي﴾ The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the speaker is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿ماذا﴾ An interrogative noun, mafʿūl bihi of خلق placed first. ﴿خَلَقَ الَّذِينَ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the interrogative clause stands in place of the second and third mafʿūls of أروني. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [verb that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿بَلِ﴾ A particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ The khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of ضلال; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ The wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, the lām falls in the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْنا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لُقْمانَ﴾ First mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْحِكْمَةَ﴾ Second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنِ اشْكُرْ﴾ an is explicative (mufassira), redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is explicative and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿مَنْ﴾ A jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَشْكُرْ﴾ An imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); إنما is the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يَشْكُرْ﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the two clauses of protasis and apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من, and the clause من.. is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿مَنْ﴾ A jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرَ﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ The fāʾ is connective, and a particle resembling the verb, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾ Two khabars; the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the two clauses of protasis and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause من is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿إِذْ﴾ An adverb of time. ﴿قالَ لُقْمانُ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لِابْنِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَعِظُهُ﴾ An imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يا بُنَيَّ﴾ A vocative particle and the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf). ﴿لا تُشْرِكْ﴾ An imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the two clauses, the vocative and the verbal, are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ﴾ inna and its ism. ﴿لَظُلْمٌ﴾ The shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and its khabar. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa); the nominal clause is a causation (taʿlīl) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا﴾ The wāw is the wāw of parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِوالِدَيْهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ﴾ A past verb and its mafʿūl. ﴿أُمُّهُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is parenthetical and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَهْناً﴾ A substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object). ﴿عَلى وَهْنٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَفِصالُهُ﴾ The wāw is parenthetical, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي عامَيْنِ﴾ The khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is parenthetical and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنِ اشْكُرْ﴾ an is explicative (mufassira), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is explicative. ﴿لِي﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَلِوالِدَيْكَ﴾ [A preposition and its genitive noun] conjoined to لي. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ khabar placed first. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ placed after; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿جاهَداكَ﴾ A past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿عَلى﴾ A preposition. ﴿أَنْ تُشْرِكَ﴾ An imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of genitive by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاهداك. ﴿بِي﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ما لَيْسَ﴾ mā is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَكَ﴾ Its khabar (predicate), placed first. ﴿بِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to علم. ﴿عِلْمٌ﴾ The ism of laysa, placed after; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿فَلا تُطِعْهُما﴾ The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وما﴾ [i.e. the mā of ـهما] marks the dual; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿صاحِبْهُما﴾ An imperative verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مَعْرُوفاً﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَاتَّبِعْ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿سَبِيلَ مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi annexed to من; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنابَ﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila of من. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ A conjunction. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ khabar placed first. ﴿مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ The fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِما﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its ism. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ An imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم.. is the ṣila.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿يا بُنَيَّ﴾ yā is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf). ﴿إِنَّها﴾ inna and its ism. ﴿إِنْ﴾ A jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَكُ﴾ A defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the sign of its jussive is the sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightening, and its ism is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِثْقالَ﴾ The khabar (predicate) of تك. ﴿حَبَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position, and the vocative clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of حبة. ﴿فَتَكُنْ﴾ The fāʾ is a conjunction, and a defective imperfect verb whose ism is latent. ﴿فِي صَخْرَةٍ﴾ The khabar of تكن; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَوْ﴾ A conjunction. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, conjoined to في صخرة. ﴿أَوْ﴾ A conjunction. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, conjoined to في السموات. ﴿يَأْتِ﴾ An imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿بِهَا اللَّهُ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the Divine Name is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its ism. ﴿لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾ Two khabars; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. And in [the conditional particle] together with what it governs is the khabar of إنها.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿يا بُنَيَّ﴾ yā is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf). ﴿أَقِمِ﴾ An imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الصَّلاةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ Conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ﴾ An imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاصْبِرْ﴾ An imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَصابَكَ﴾ A past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿إِنَّ ذلِكَ﴾ inna and its ism. ﴿مِنْ عَزْمِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْأُمُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the verse is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿هُدىً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿وَرَحْمَةً﴾ Conjoined to هدى. ﴿لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) رحمة.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ The relative noun is an adjective (ṣifa) of المحسنين. ﴿يُقِيمُونَ﴾ An imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الصَّلاةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ﴾ Conjoined to يقيمون الصلاة. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يوقنون. ﴿هُمْ﴾ A pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾ An imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of هم, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ The demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلى هُدىً﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to هدى. ﴿وَأُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ A pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ The preposition and its genitive noun are a khabar (predicate) placed first. ﴿مِنَ﴾ [Translator's note: the source prints ﴿مِنَ﴾ here; the word of the verse is مَنْ.] A relative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَشْتَرِي﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) annexed to الحديث; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِيُضِلَّ﴾ An imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يشتري. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb, and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَها﴾ An imperfect verb conjoined to ليضل, and hā is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿هُزُواً﴾ Second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ khabar placed first. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ placed after. ﴿مُهِينٌ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of عذاب; the clause is the khabar of أولئك, and the clause أولئك.. is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿إِذا﴾ A non-jussive conditional adverb (ẓarfiyya sharṭiyya ghayr jāzima). ﴿تُتْلى﴾ A passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿آياتُنا﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿وَلَّى﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مُسْتَكْبِراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿كَأَنْ﴾ Lightened from the heavy [كأن] (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its ism is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَمْ يَسْمَعْها﴾ An imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and hā is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of كأن, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿كَأَنْ﴾ A particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl). ﴿فِي أُذُنَيْهِ﴾ The khabar of كأن, placed first. ﴿وَقْراً﴾ Its ism, placed after; the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُ﴾ The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِعَذابٍ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of عذاب.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its ism. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ Conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ﴾ A khabar (predicate) placed first and a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after. ﴿النَّعِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الذين.. is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِيها﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خالدين. ﴿وَعْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿حَقًّا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ A mubtadaʾ (subject) and two khabars (predicates); the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿وَلا تُصَعِّرْ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿خَدَّكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تَمْشِ﴾ Conjoined to ولا تصعر. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مَرَحاً﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿لا يُحِبُّ﴾ [lā is] negating, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مُخْتالٍ﴾ An adjective of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being "a servant who is arrogant (عبد مختال)". ﴿فَخُورٍ﴾ A second adjective; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is a causation (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَاقْصِدْ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿فِي مَشْيِكَ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاغْضُضْ مِنْ صَوْتِكَ﴾ Conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ أَنْكَرَ﴾ inna and its ism. ﴿الْأَصْواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَصَوْتُ﴾ The shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿صوت الْحَمِيرِ﴾ The khabar (predicate) of inna, annexed to الحمير; the nominal clause is a causation (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَوْا﴾ The hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿سَخَّرَ﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna, its ism and its khabar stands in place of the two mafʿūls of تروا. ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ Conjoined to ما في السموات. ﴿وَأَسْبَغَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿نِعَمَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ظاهِرَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَباطِنَةً﴾ Conjoined to ظاهرة; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ The wāw is a resumptive particle, and a khabar placed first. ﴿مِنَ﴾ [Translator's note: the source prints ﴿مِنَ﴾ here; the word of the verse is مَنْ.] mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿يُجادِلُ﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلا هُدىً﴾ Conjoined to بغير علم. ﴿وَلا كِتابٍ﴾ Conjoined to بغير علم. ﴿مُنِيرٍ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of كتاب.

daas-irab:21-21.t:
﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿إِذا﴾ A non-jussive conditional adverb (ẓarfiyya sharṭiyya ghayr jāzima). ﴿قِيلَ﴾ A passive past verb. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿اتَّبِعُوا﴾ An imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of قيل. ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ A past verb, and the Divine Name is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿قالُوا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿بَلْ﴾ A particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿نَتَّبِعُ﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَجَدْنا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿آباءَنا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. The clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿أَوَلَوْ﴾ The hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لَوْ﴾ A non-jussive conditional, and its apodosis is omitted. ﴿كانَ الشَّيْطانُ﴾ kāna and its ism. ﴿يَدْعُوهُمْ﴾ An imperfect verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause كان..
is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلى عَذابِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿السَّعِيرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿مَنْ﴾ A jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُسْلِمْ﴾ An imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿وَجْهَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿هُوَ مُحْسِنٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَقَدِ﴾ The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿اسْتَمْسَكَ﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِالْعُرْوَةِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْوُثْقى﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of العروة; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the two clauses of protasis and apodosis are the khabar, and the clause من.. is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ khabar placed first. ﴿عاقِبَةُ﴾ mubtadaʾ placed after. ﴿الْأُمُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿مَنْ﴾ A jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرَ﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿فَلا يَحْزُنْكَ﴾ The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿كُفْرُهُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿إِلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهُمْ﴾ A khabar (predicate) placed first and a mubtadaʾ placed after; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَنُنَبِّئُهُمْ﴾ The fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِما﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ Its khabar. ﴿بِذاتِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عليم. ﴿الصُّدُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. The two clauses of protasis and apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من, and the clause من.. is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿نُمَتِّعُهُمْ﴾ An imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ A conjunction. ﴿نَضْطَرُّهُمْ﴾ An imperfect verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلى عَذابٍ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿غَلِيظٍ﴾ An adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ The wāw is a resumptive particle, the lām is the one preparing for an omitted oath (mawṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and in is a jussive conditional particle. ﴿سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ A past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿مَنْ﴾ An interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ A past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ Conjoined to السموات; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of من, and the clause من خلق.. is the second mafʿūl bihi of سأل. ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ The lām falls in the answer to the oath, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the dropped wāw of the plural is the fāʿil, and the nūn is a particle of emphasis with no grammatical position; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ The Divine Name is the fāʿil of an omitted verb; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قُلِ﴾ An imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ The Divine Name and the preposition are the khabar; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿بَلْ﴾ A particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ The preposition and the Divine Name in the genitive are a khabar (predicate) placed first. ﴿ما﴾ A relative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ Conjoined to السموات. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿هُوَ﴾ A pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ﴾ Two khabars of inna; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿لَوْ﴾ A non-jussive conditional. ﴿أَنَّ﴾ A particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl). ﴿ما﴾ The ism of anna. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَقْلامٌ﴾ The khabar (predicate) of anna; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna, its ism and its khabar is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb which what follows explains. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿وَالْبَحْرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَمُدُّهُ﴾ An imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is the khabar of البحر, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍ﴾ fāʿil, annexed to أبحر. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿نَفِدَتْ كَلِماتُ اللَّهِ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil, and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the answer of law and has no grammatical position [Translator's note: the source reads «جواب لولا محل لها», evidently «جواب لو لا محل لها» run together]. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ Two khabars; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿خَلْقُكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا بَعْثُكُمْ﴾ Conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ A particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿كَنَفْسٍ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of بعثكم. ﴿واحِدَةٍ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of نفس. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ﴾ inna, its ism and its two khabars; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ The hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿يُولِجُ﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿اللَّيْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِي النَّهارِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna, its ism and its khabar stands in place of the two mafʿūls of ترى. ﴿وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ Conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ﴾ Conjoined as well. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَجْرِي﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلى أَجَلٍ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُسَمًّى﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of أجل. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction, and anna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿بِما﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ An imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. The interpreted maṣdar formed from anna, its ism and its khabar is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ The demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition; and anna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿هُوَ﴾ A pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ The khabar (predicate) of anna; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna, its ism and its khabar is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿أَنَّ ما﴾ anna and its ism. ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ An imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْباطِلُ﴾ The khabar of anna; the interpreted maṣdar formed from anna, its ism and its khabar is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿هُوَ﴾ A pronoun of separation. ﴿الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ﴾ Two khabars of anna; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ The hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنَّ الْفُلْكَ﴾ anna and its ism. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna, its ism and its khabar stands in place of the two mafʿūls of تر. ﴿فِي الْبَحْرِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿بِنِعْمَتِ اللَّهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb as well, and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لِيُرِيَكُمْ﴾ An imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تجري. ﴿مِنْ آياتِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَنَّ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the word of the verse is إِنَّ, and the analysis that follows treats it as inna.] A particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl). ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ The khabar of inna, placed first; and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿لَآياتٍ﴾ The ism of inna, placed after; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of آيات. ﴿صَبَّارٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and it is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun. ﴿شَكُورٍ﴾ A second adjective.

daas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿إِذا غَشِيَهُمْ﴾ iḏā is a non-jussive conditional adverb (ẓarfiyya sharṭiyya ghayr jāzima), and a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿مَوْجٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿كَالظُّلَلِ﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of موج. ﴿دَعَوُا اللَّهَ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil, and the Divine Name is its mafʿūl; the clause is the answer of iḏā and has no grammatical position. ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَهُ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them. ﴿الدِّينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ The fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿لما﴾ A conditional adverb. ﴿نَجَّاهُمْ﴾ A past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ﴾ The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa). ﴿منهم﴾ A khabar (predicate) placed first. ﴿مُقْتَصِدٌ﴾ A mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿وَما﴾ negating. ﴿يَجْحَدُ﴾ An imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ A particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿كُلُّ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿خَتَّارٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and it is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "a treacherous servant (عبد ختار)". ﴿كَفُورٍ﴾ A second adjective; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:33-33.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ A vocative particle and the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda). ﴿النَّاسُ﴾ badal (substitute); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿اتَّقُوا﴾ An imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبَّكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاخْشَوْا﴾ Conjoined to اتقوا. ﴿يَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَجْزِي والِدٌ﴾ An imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَنْ وَلَدِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of يوما. ﴿وَ﴾ The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿مَوْلُودٌ﴾
Conjoined to والد. ﴿هُوَ جازٍ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is an adjective of مولود. ﴿عَنْ والِدِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جاز. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ inna and its ism, annexed to the Divine Name. ﴿حَقٌّ﴾ Its khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَلا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ﴾ The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْحَياةُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ An adjective of الحياة; the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ﴾ Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿عِنْدَهُ﴾ An adverb of place, a khabar (predicate) placed first. ﴿عِلْمُ﴾ A mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الله ... is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿السَّاعَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْغَيْثَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ﴾ Conjoined to ينزل. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي الْأَرْحامِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ﴾ An imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿ماذا﴾ An interrogative noun, a mafʿūl bihi placed first. ﴿تَكْسِبُ﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿غَداً﴾ An adverb of time; the clause stands in place of the two mafʿūls of تدري. The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ﴾ An imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِأَيِّ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تموت. ﴿أَرْضٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تَمُوتُ﴾ An imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl of تدري. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Divine Name is its ism. ﴿عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾ Its two khabars; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:16-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خَرْدَلٍ): al-khardal (mustard) is a plant with very small, black, pungent seeds; the singular is khardala. One says "khardala al-ṭaʿām" (he ate the choicest of the food), and "khardala al-laḥm" (he cut its limbs into many small pieces); "laḥm kharādīl" means meat cut up and separated. It is proverbial for smallness. This has already been discussed in [Surat] al-Anbiyāʾ.
(وَلا تُصَعِّرْ): do not turn your face away out of arrogance. Abū ʿUbayda said: the original meaning of al-ṣaʿar is a disease that afflicts the camel (al-baṣīr) [Translator's note: the text reads «البصير»; al-baʿīr "the camel" seems intended] and twists its neck. Since that may happen for one of various passing purposes, He indicated what is meant by saying "to people" (li-l-nās), with the lām of cause, i.e. do not do that for the sake of turning away from them. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-ṣaʿar, with two fatḥas, is a tilt in the neck and a turning of the face towards one of the two sides of the mouth. A person may be aṣʿar by creation, or something else may make him so by something that befalls him. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of the pattern of taʿiba. Ṣaʿʿara khaddahu, with the doubled letter, and ṣāʿarahu, mean he turned it away from people in aversion and arrogance." In al-Asās: "In his neck and his cheek there is ṣaʿar: a tilt from arrogance. One says: 'I shall surely straighten your ṣaʿar.' And one says: 'In his eye there is ṣawar, and in his cheek ṣaʿar,' and he is aṣʿar; ṣaʿʿara khaddahu and ṣāʿarahu; 'do not tilt (lā tuṣāʿir) your cheek'; so-and-so is mutaṣāʿir, and he has become haughty (taṣāʿara). Ḥassān said:
ألسنا نذود المعلمين لدى الوغى ... ذيادا يسلّي نخوة المتصاعر
(Do we not drive back the marked champions in battle, a driving-back that dispels the pride of the haughty one?)
Ostriches are ṣuʿr by creation, and camels tilt their heads (taṣāʿar) in their nose-rings. In the ḥadīth: 'A time will come upon people when there will be among them none but the one who turns his cheek in pride (aṣʿar) or the one cut off (abtar).'
The ṣād together with the ʿayn, as the first and second radicals of a word, has the particular sense of insolence and haughtiness. One says: a difficult (ṣaʿb) matter, a difficult plan, a difficult mountain path — it is one of the difficult paths — and he fell into difficult plans; and the insolence and haughtiness in that is not hidden. Aṣʿaba al-jamal: the camel was not ridden and no rope had touched it, so it is muṣʿab. Among the figurative uses of this root: so-and-so is a muṣʿab among the maṣāʿib (an unbroken stallion, i.e. a chief), as you say 'a qarm among the qurūm' (a stallion among stallions). One says ṣaʿida al-saṭḥ and ṣaʿida ilā al-saṭḥ (he climbed the roof / up to the roof), ṣaʿida fī al-sullam (on the ladder) and in the sky, taṣaʿʿada and taṣāʿada, and ṣaʿʿada fī al-jabal (he climbed the mountain); 'my descending and ascending in the land took long'; aṣʿada fī al-arḍ: he went towards land higher than the other; aṣʿadat al-safīna: its sail was spread and the wind carried it off; 'ʿalayka bi-l-ṣaʿīd' means sit on the ground; ṣaʿīd al-arḍ is its surface; tanaffasa al-ṣuʿadāʾ: his breath rose high (he sighed deeply); the arrow went upwards (ṣaʿadan); and it is as though his stature were a ṣaʿda, which is the cane that grows straight. Al-Aḥnaf said:
إن على كل رئيس حقّا ... أن يخضب الصّعدة أو تندقّا
(Every chief has a duty: to dye the spear-shaft [with blood] or have it shatter.)
Among the figurative uses: he has rising (ṣāʿid) nobility and helping fortune; his rank is far to climb (baʿīdat al-maṣʿad and al-maṣāʿid); a ṣāʿid neck is a long one; a ṣaʿda girl is one of straight stature, and the plural is ṣaʿdāt with sukūn; 'he took a hundred and upwards (fa-ṣāʿidan)' meaning 'and more'; and 'I burdened him with ṣaʿūd' means I loaded him with hardship.
The ṣaʿāfiqa are those who attend the market without capital, and when someone buys something they join him in it. Ṣaʿaqathum al-samāʾ and aṣʿaqathum: the sky struck them with a ṣāʿiqa (thunderbolt), which is a fire that passes by nothing without burning it, with a violent crash. Al-ṣaʿlaka is well known: it is poverty and going far off in the land. Abū Dāwūd said:
مثل عير الفلاة صعلكه البقل مشيح بأربع عسرات
(Like the wild ass of the desert, made lean by the herbage, urging on four difficult ones) — four she-asses. And Dhū al-Rumma said:
تخيل في المرعى لهنّ بشخصه ... مصعلك أعلى قلّة الرأس نقنق
(A small-headed (muṣaʿlak) male ostrich, with the top of its head bare, shows itself to them in the pasture.)"
(وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ): i.e. be moderate in it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And be even in it, so that it is a walk between two walks: do not creep like those who feign weakness (al-mutamāwitūn, lit. those who act as if dying), nor leap like the rogues. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Fast walking takes away the splendour of the believer.' As for ʿĀʾisha's saying about ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, 'When he walked, he walked quickly,' she meant only a speed above the creeping of one who feigns weakness."
(وَاغْضُضْ مِنْ طرفك) [Translator's note: the source writes «من طرفك» here; the verse reads ﴿مِنْ صَوْتِكَ﴾]: and lower it and shorten it — from your saying "so-and-so yaghuḍḍu min so-and-so" when he belittles him and lowers him. In al-Asās: "Wa-ghḍuḍ min ṣawtika: lower it. Ghuḍḍa ṭarfaka: lower your gaze; a lowered (ghaḍīḍ) gaze. Ghuḍḍa min lijāmi farasika: pull down your horse's bridle and lower it to reduce its vehemence. Ighḍuḍ lī sāʿatan: hold back your mount for me and stop for me. Al-Jaʿdī said:
خليلي غضّا ساعة وتهجرا
(My two friends, halt a while, then travel in the midday heat) — i.e. hold back your mounts for me a while, then set off travelling in the midday heat. So-and-so is ghaḍīḍ: lowly, with evident abasement (ghaḍāḍa); 'there is ghaḍāḍa for you in this, so do not do it'; and 'ghaḍāḍa reached him from such-and-such', i.e. deficiency and blame."

* I'rab:
(يا بُنَيَّ إِنَّها إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ): the i'rab of (يا بني) has been given many times; this is part of the remainder of Luqmān's counsel. (إنّ) and its noun; (إن) is conditional; (تك) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of the jussive being the sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn that was dropped for lightening. The noun of (تك) is latent (mustatir), referring to the sin. That is because Luqmān's son said: "O my father, if I commit a sin where no one knows of it, how will Allah know of it?" So he said: "O my son, if it be the weight of a grain of the kind of mustard…" (مثقال) is the predicate of (تك); (حبة) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من خردل) is an adjective (ṣifa) of (حبة), i.e. it were like a mustard grain in smallness and insignificance.
(فَتَكُنْ فِي صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِي السَّماواتِ أَوْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَأْتِ بِهَا اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ): (فتكن) is conjoined to (تك); the noun of (تكن) is latent, its implied form being "it", i.e. the sin, the small misdeed; (في صخرة) is the predicate of (تكن); (أو في السموات أو في الأرض) is conjoined to (في صخرة), i.e. in the most hidden place among the three mentioned. (يأت) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (بها) — preposition and its genitive noun — is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأت); (الله) is the fāʿil (agent); and (إنّ), its noun and its two predicates.
(يا بُنَيَّ أَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ): (أقم) is an imperative verb, its agent obligatorily latent, its implied form being "you" (anta); (الصلاة) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (وأمر بالمعروف) is conjoined, and likewise (وانه عن المنكر).
(وَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما أَصابَكَ إِنَّ ذلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ): (إنّ), its fronted predicate and its postponed noun. The meaning of (عزم الأمور) is: of the things resolved upon; so it is a maṣdar in the sense of the passive participle, or in the sense of the active participle, i.e. of the resolving matters, i.e. of what Allah has made a firm resolve and made obligatory upon His servants.
(وَلا تُصَعِّرْ خَدَّكَ لِلنَّاسِ وَلا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحاً): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تصعر) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا), its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (للناس) is attached to (تصعر); (ولا تمش) is conjoined to (ولا تصعر); (في الأرض) is attached to (تمش); (مرحا) is a maṣdar occupying the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "an exultant walking", or mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. do not walk for the sake of exultation and insolence.
Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "He meant: and do not walk exulting exultantly; or He put the maṣdar in the place of the ḥāl in the sense of 'exulting'; and it may be meant: for the sake of exultation and insolence."
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ): (إنّ) and its noun; the clause (لا يحب) is its predicate; (كل) is the object of (يحب); and (فخور) is conjoined to (مختال). [Translator's note: (فخور) is so described in the source; it is ordinarily parsed as a second adjective.]
(وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَاغْضُضْ مِنْ صَوْتِكَ): the wāw is conjunctive; (اقصد) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (في مشيك) is attached to (أقصر) [Translator's note: so in the source; (اقصد) is meant]; (واغضض من صوتك) is conjoined to what precedes.
(إِنَّ أَنْكَرَ الْأَصْواتِ لَصَوْتُ الْحَمِيرِ): the clause gives the reason for the command to lower the voice, in an emphatic form, as will come in the section on rhetoric. (إنّ) and its noun; (الأصوات) is muḍāf ilayhi; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; and (صوت الحمير) is the predicate of (إنّ).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل» to the end of the verse there is the device of al-tamām or al-tatmīm (completion), which has been pointed out in places in this book. The meaning is that He completed the hiddenness of the small misdeed or sin in itself with the hiddenness of its place, the rock; and more hidden than a rock is that it be in a rock settled in the remote depths of the earth, or in the heights of the expanses of space. An example of it in poetry is the saying of al-Khansāʾ:
وإن صخرا لتأتمّ الهداة به ... كأنه علم في رأسه نار
(Truly Ṣakhr is one whom the guides follow, as though he were a mountain with a fire on its peak.)
Her saying "with a fire on its peak" is a beautiful, indispensable completion, embodying prominence and renown for those travelling by night and by morning.
And the saying of ʿAntara al-ʿAbsī:
أثني عليّ بما علمت فإنني ... سهل مخالقتي إذا لم أظلم
(Praise me for what you know [of me], for I am easy to get along with when I am not wronged.)
His saying "when I am not wronged" is a fine completion.
Among fine completions is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays describing the horse:
على هيكل يعطيك قبل سؤاله ... أفانين جري غير كزّ ولا واني
(On a massive steed that gives you, before you ask it, all kinds of running, neither stiff nor flagging.)
His saying "before you ask it" is a wonderful completion of his saying "all kinds of running". And how beautiful is the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā on this topic:
من يلق يوما على علاته هرما ... يلق السماحة منه والندى خلقا
(Whoever meets Harim one day, whatever his state, finds generosity and liberality to be his nature.)
The completion here is in his saying "whatever his state", and it is a wonderful completion containing a still more wonderful hyperbole. In the same vein runs the saying of Ibn Miḥkān al-Saʿdī when he was brought forward to be killed:
ولست- وإن كانت إليّ حبيبة- بباك على الدنيا إذا ما تولت
(I am not — even though it is dear to me — one to weep over this world when it turns away.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad said: he made an exception, "even though it is dear to me", a charming exception, and he intended [the order of] fronting and postponing; therefore it was permissible for him to bring the pronoun before its overt referent.
2- Emphasis with inna, and other devices:
Among the beauties of this verse, «إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير», are several devices to which we point:
a- He brought the comparison emphasised first with inna, and reinforced this emphasis with the lām, so the speech became a khabar inkārī (a statement addressed to a denier), as though the comparison were a settled matter into which doubt does not enter. Inna may enter the clause, and you see the speech with it as resumptive and not resumptive, cut off and joined at the same time; and using it in this way requires both reflection and deliberation. The secret of this usage was hidden even from the outstanding scholars. It is related that al-Aṣmaʿī said: I used to go with Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and Khalaf al-Aḥmar, and they would come to Bashshār and greet him with the utmost reverence, then say: "O Abū Muʿādh, what have you newly composed?" He would tell them and recite to them, and they would ask him and write from him, humble before him, until the time of noon came, and then they would leave. They came to him one day and said: "What is this ode that you composed about Salm ibn Qutayba?" He said: "It is the one that has reached you." They said: "It has reached us that you used many rare words in it." He said: "Yes; it reached me that Salm ibn Qutayba affects expertise in rare words, so I wanted to present him with what he does not know." They said: "Then recite it to us, O Abū Muʿādh." So he recited to them:
بكّرا يا صاحبيّ قبل الهجير ... إن ذاك النجاح في التبكير
(Set off early, my two companions, before the midday heat; truly success lies in setting off early.)
until he finished it. Khalaf said to him: "Had you said, O Abū Muʿādh, instead of 'إن ذاك النجاح في التبكير', 'بكّرا فالنجاح في التبكير' (set off early, for success lies in setting off early), it would have been better." Bashshār said: "I built it only in a wild Bedouin style, so I said 'إن ذاك النجاح في التبكير' as the desert Bedouins say. Had I said 'بكرا في النجاح' [Translator's note: so in the source; «فالنجاح» is evidently meant], it would have been the speech of the muwalladūn (post-classical poets), and would not resemble that speech or enter into the meaning of the ode." He said: so Khalaf rose and kissed him between the eyes. ʿAbd al-Qāhir said in his comment on this story: "Was this remark from Khalaf and the criticism of Bashshār anything but due to the subtlety of the meaning in it and its hiddenness?"
ʿAbd al-Qāhir went on in his analysis of Bashshār's verse and said: As for the clause being resumptive with inna, that is because it is not conjoined to what precedes it with the wāw, and it occurs in answer to an implied question, as though a questioner asked: "And why does he ask his two companions to set off early before the midday heat?" and the answer was: "Truly success lies in setting off early." As for its joining its clause to the previous clause, the proof of that is that if you dropped "inna" from the clause you would see the second clause not connect with the first and have no relation to it until you bring the fāʾ, saying: "Set off early, my two companions, before the midday heat, for (fa-) success lies in setting off early." Perhaps that is the secret of its subtlety and fineness and of the forcefulness of expression with it, and it is the mark of the wild Bedouin construction — the opposite of what it would be had he said "Set off early, for success lies in setting off early", which is an easy construction, clearly connected by the fāʾ, and that is the mark of clause construction among the muwalladūn. And while the fāʾ gives connection, it does not give the emphasis that "inna" indicates. This forceful construction is what has come in the Qur'an to an extent beyond counting.
ʿAbd al-Qāhir relates in Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz the story of Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq al-Kindī, the philosophiser, when he rode to Abū al-ʿAbbās and said to him: "I find padding in the speech of the Arabs." Abū al-ʿAbbās said to him: "In what place have you found that?" He said: "I find the Arabs saying 'ʿAbdullāh qāʾim' (ʿAbdullāh is standing), then saying 'inna ʿAbdullāh qāʾim', then saying 'inna ʿAbdullāh la-qāʾim'; so the words are repeated while the meaning is one."
[Translator's note: the source here repeats a fragment: «كلام العرب حشوا فقال أبو العباس: في أي موضوع وجدت ذلك؟» ("…padding in the speech of the Arabs. Abū al-ʿAbbās said: In what place have you found that?"), evidently a duplicated line.]
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: "Rather, the meanings differ because the words differ. Their saying 'ʿAbdullāh qāʾim' is a report of his standing; their saying 'inna ʿAbdullāh qāʾim' is an answer to a questioner's question; and their saying 'inna ʿAbdullāh la-qāʾim' is an answer to the denial of one who denies his standing. So the words have been repeated because the meanings are repeated."
We have quoted at length only because of the subtlety and hiddenness of this discussion; and in the verse before us it occurs in the most beautiful and subtle position, clarifying the reason for the command to lower the voice, built on likening those who raise their voices to donkeys and representing their voices as braying, and going to the utmost in deterring from raising the voice. Al-Khaṭīb [al-Shirbīnī] excelled in explaining this reason, and we quote his passage at length for its splendour and originality. He said:
"If it is asked: why did He mention what prevents raising the voice and not mention what prevents walking fast? It is answered that raising the voice harms the hearer and strikes the ear canal with its force, and may perhaps tear the membrane inside the ear; whereas walking fast does not harm, and if it does harm, it harms only whoever is in one's path, while the voice reaches whoever is on the right and on the left. Also because walking harms the organ of walking, while the voice harms the organ of hearing, and the organ of hearing is at the door of the heart, for speech is carried from hearing to the heart, which is not so with walking. Also, ugly speech is uglier than ugly action, and its good is better, because the tongue is the interpreter of the heart. And since raising the voice beyond need is objectionable, just as lowering it below need is considered feigned weakness and arrogance, and He had indicated the prohibition of this with (من), conveying that both extremes are blameworthy, He gave the reason for prohibiting the first by His saying 'Truly the most objectionable', i.e. the most hideous and repugnant, 'of voices', by raising them beyond need, 'is the voice of donkeys', i.e. of this kind, because of its excessive loudness without need. For of every animal one may understand from its voice that it cries out from a heavy load or fatigue, like the camel, or for some other reason; but the donkey, if it died under its load, would not cry out, and if it were killed, would not cry out, and at some times when there is no need it cries out and brays with a voice whose beginning is an in-drawn wheeze and whose end is an in-drawn wheeze."
b- The singular "voice":
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Why did He make the voice of the donkeys singular and not plural? I say: what is meant is not to mention the voice of each individual of this kind so that it would be made plural; what is meant is only that every kind of animal [Translator's note: the source reads «الحيوان الناطق» "rational animal", which seems a slip for «الحيوان» alone] has a voice, and the most objectionable of the voices of these kinds is the voice of this kind; so it had to be singular."
Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya):
In this verse there is explicit metaphor, in that the speech has been emptied of the word of comparison and brought out in the form of metaphor: they were made donkeys and their voice made braying, as an intensification of censure and disparagement and an extreme of prohibiting raising the voice. The donkey is proverbial for eloquent censure and painful insult, and likewise its braying.
Among their regarding the mere mention of it as obscene and their avoiding its name is that they allude to it by metonymy and decline to state it explicitly, saying "the long-eared one". It is related that ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd the scribe said: "Do not ride the donkey, for if it is lively it tires your hand, and if it is sluggish it tires your foot." A Bedouin said: "What a bad mount is the donkey! If you stop it, it lets down [its member]; if you leave it, it turns away; much dung, little help; quick to flee, slow in the raid; blood is not protected by it, women are not given as dowry with it, and it is not milked into the vessel." And among the Arabs there are those who never ride it, even if need and hardship drive them to it.
"Voice" is a maṣdar:
In al-Qurṭubī: "(لصوت الحمير): the lām is for emphasis. He made 'voice' singular even though it is annexed to a group because it is a maṣdar, and the maṣdar indicates multiplicity. It is the maṣdar of ṣāta yaṣūtu ṣawtan, so he is ṣāʾit; and one says ṣawwata taṣwītan, so he is muṣawwit; and a ṣāt man, i.e. one with a loud voice, in the sense of ṣāʾit."

dervis-irab:20-24.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَأَسْبَغَ): and He completed. One says: asbagha Allāhu ʿalayhi al-niʿma, He completed the favour upon him; asbagha al-thawb: he made the garment ample and long; asbagha al-rajul: the man put on an ample coat of mail; asbagha lahu al-nafaqa: he was generous with him in provision and spent on him the full amount he needed. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Sabaghat al-niʿma subūghan: the favour became ample; Allah asbaghahā: He poured it out and completed it; asbaghtu al-wuḍūʾ: I completed the ablution." It has been read with sīn and with ṣād; and so it is with every sīn that comes together with ghayn, khāʾ or qāf: you say ṣalakha for salakha, ṣaqar for saqar, and ṣāligh for sāligh. The meaning of sāligh is from salaghat al-baqara wa-l-shāt, when the cow or the ewe sheds the tooth that comes after the sadīs [Translator's note: so in the source, «التي خلقت السديس», probably «خَلَفَت» "that follows"]; al-sulūgh in cloven-hoofed animals corresponds to al-buzūl (the cutting of the ninth-year tooth) in animals with … [Translator's note: the source reads «ذوات الأحقاف»; «ذوات الأخفاف» "animals with padded feet", i.e. camels, seems intended].
(بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقى): the following came in al-Qāmūs: "al-ʿurwa of the bucket and the jug is the handle; of the garment, the counterpart of its button (the loop), like al-ʿurā, and it is also pronounced with kasra; of the private part, the flesh of its outside that widens and extends right and left along the lower part of the clitoris, and a farj muʿarrā [is one having this]; the group of thorny trees and saltbush that is grazed in drought; the lion; the dense trees in which camels winter and eat from them, or whose leaves do not fall in winter; the precious among wealth, like the noble horse; and the patrons of the land." In al-Asās and al-Lisān: "Al-ʿurwa is borrowed for what one holds firmly to and relies upon. So it is said of precious wealth and the noble horse: 'so-and-so has a ʿurwa'; and the camels have a ʿurwa of herbage and a ʿulqa: for a remnant of it that remains after the plants have dried up, to which they cling because it is a safeguard for them that they resort to when other plants have been eaten. Labīd said:
خلع الملوك وسار تحت لوائه ... شجر العرا وعراعر الأقوام
(He deposed kings, and under his banner marched the 'trees of al-ʿurā' and the chiefs of the peoples.)
i.e. they are safeguards for people, like the thorny trees with which livestock is safeguarded. The commanders of an army are called al-ʿurā, and the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, are the ʿurā of Islam. And the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
كأن عرا المرجان منها تعلّقت ... على أمّ خشف من ظباء المشاقر
(As though the loops of coral from her had been hung on the mother of a fawn among the gazelles of al-Mashāqir.)
by al-ʿurā he meant the necklaces… And al-ʿurwa is one of the names of the lion."

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُمْ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ): resumptive speech, returning to the address to the polytheists that came before the story of Luqmān and his counsel. The hamza is for the rebuking, disapproving question; the wāw conjoins to the previous address to them; (لم) is a particle of negation, transformation [of tense] and the jussive; (تروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). The seeing is mental, and (أنّ) with what lies in its domain stands in place of the two objects of (تروا). (أنّ) and its noun; the clause (سخر) is its predicate; (لكم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سخر); (ما) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (في السموات) is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما); and (ما في الأرض) is conjoined to (ما في السموات).
(وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظاهِرَةً وَباطِنَةً): (وأسبغ) is conjoined to (سخر); (عليكم) is attached to (أسبغ); (نعمه) is the direct object; (ظاهرة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (باطنة) is conjoined to (ظاهرة). The meaning of "outward" and "inward" will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلا هُدىً وَلا كِتابٍ مُنِيرٍ): the wāw is resumptive; (من الناس) is a fronted khabar (predicate) and (من) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يجادل) is the ṣila of (من) if it is a relative, or an adjective of it if it is a complete indefinite in the sense of "people"; (في الله) is attached to (يجادل), i.e. concerning His oneness and His attributes; (بغير علم) is a ḥāl; (ولا هدى) is conjoined; and (ولا كتاب منير) is conjoined to (علم).
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ ما وَجَدْنا عَلَيْهِ آباءَنا): the wāw is conjunctive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (فيل) [Translator's note: so in the source; (قيل) is meant] is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (لهم) is attached to (قيل); the clause (اتبعوا) is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl); (ما) is the direct object; the clause (أنزل الله) is the ṣila; the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; (نتبع) is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we"; (ما) is the direct object; the clause (وجدنا) is the ṣila; (عليه) is attached to (وجدنا), or to an omitted element which is the second object of (وجدنا); and (آباءنا) is the first object of (وجدنا), i.e. we found our fathers devoted to it.
(أَوَلَوْ كانَ الشَّيْطانُ يَدْعُوهُمْ إِلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ): the hamza is for the rebuking, disapproving question. The wāw has two possibilities: one, that it conjoins to something omitted; the second, that it is circumstantial. In either case an omitted element must be supplied, its meaning being: "Will they follow him even if Satan is calling them?" (لو) is conditional and its apodosis is omitted, i.e. "he calls them and they follow"; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (كان الشيطان): (كان) and its noun; the clause (يدعوهم) is its predicate; and (إلى عذاب السعير) is attached to (يدعوهم).
(وَمَنْ يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقى): the wāw is conjunctive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يسلم) is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its agent latent, its implied form being "he"; (وجهه) is the direct object; (إلى الله) is attached to (يسلم). (يسلم) is made transitive with the lām, but here it is made transitive with (إلى) so that its meaning is that he handed himself over, as goods are handed over to a man when they are delivered to him; what is meant is reliance upon Him and entrusting [one's affairs] to Him. The wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl; (هو) is mubtadaʾ and (محسن) predicate. (فقد): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and (قد) is a particle of realisation; (استمسك) is a past verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "he"; (بالعروة) — preposition and its genitive noun — is attached to (استمسك); (الوثقى) is an adjective of (العروة); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis with its apodosis is the predicate of (من).
