(وَإِلَى اللَّهِ عاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ): (إلى الله) is a fronted predicate and (عاقبة الأمور) a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَلا يَحْزُنْكَ كُفْرُهُ): the wāw is a conjunction and the clause is conjoined to the one before it; (لا) is prohibitive; (يحزنك) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا); and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.
(إِلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهُمْ فَنُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): (إلينا) is a fronted predicate and (مرجعهم) a postponed mubtadaʾ. (فننبئهم): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (ننبئهم) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "we", and a direct object; (بما) is attached to (ننبئهم); the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila of (ما); (إنّ) and its noun; (عليم) is its predicate; and (بذات الصدور) is attached to (عليم).
(نُمَتِّعُهُمْ قَلِيلًا ثُمَّ نَضْطَرُّهُمْ إِلى عَذابٍ غَلِيظٍ): the clause (نمتعهم) may be a ḥāl from the agent of (نمتعهم) [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the agent of (ننبئهم) is meant], or resumptive. (قليلا) is an adverb, or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a little time" or "a little enjoyment". (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay; (نضطرهم) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (إلى عذاب) is attached to (نضطرهم); and (غليظ) is an adjective of (عذاب).

* Rhetoric:
1- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq):
In His saying «وأسبغ عليكم نعمه ظاهرة وباطنة» there is antithesis, which has been discussed before. By the outward favours is meant all that is known by observation, and by the inward ones what is known only by proof. Beautiful is his saying ﷺ to Ibn ʿAbbās when he asked him about this verse: "The outward is Islam and what is good in your character, and the inward is what has been concealed for you of your evil deeds." The exegetes have expanded on it at length, for which one may refer to the extensive works.
2- Representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya):
That is in His saying «فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى»: the state of the one who relies [on Allah] has been represented by the state of someone who wants to let himself down from a lofty mountain and takes precautions for himself by holding fast to the firmest loop of a strong rope whose breaking is not to be feared. It has also been said that it is a representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī), because a term of the comparison is mentioned.
3- Implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya):
In His saying «ثم نضطرهم إلى عذاب غليظ» there is implicit metaphor: their being bound to the punishment and burdened with it has been likened to the compelling of one compelled towards a thing from which he is unable to free himself, i.e. it weighs upon them with the weight of massive bodies. Thickness (al-ghilaẓ) is borrowed from thick bodies, and what is meant is severity and heaviness upon the one punished.

dervis-irab:25-27.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ): resumptive speech, introduced to show their self-contradiction and their acknowledgement of the brilliant proofs of the divine oneness that the obstinate cannot deny. The lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) is conditional; (سألتهم) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), with its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate); and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as the second object of (سألتهم). The lām occurs in the answer to the oath; (يقولن) is an imperfect verb from which the nūn of the nominative has been dropped because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw of the pronoun [dropped] because of the meeting of two sukūns; (الله) is the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is Allah", or a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is omitted, i.e. "Allah is their Creator".
(قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): (الحمد) is mubtadaʾ and (لله) predicate, and the clause is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). The command is to bind them by their acknowledgement that the One who created the heavens and the earth is Allah alone, and that praise and thanks must therefore be directed to Him. (بل) is a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī), to point out that when they are bound by that they do not hold to it and do not take heed. (أكثرهم) is mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يعلمون) its predicate.
(لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ): (لله) is a fronted predicate and (ما) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات والأرض) is the ṣila (relative clause). (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; (هو) is the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); (الغني) is its first predicate and (الحميد) its second predicate.
(وَلَوْ أَنَّما فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلامٌ): resumptive speech, introduced to point out that the meanings of His speech, glorified is He, are never exhausted. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle — further discussion of it will come in the section on benefits. (أنّ) with what follows it is the agent of an omitted verb, i.e. "if it were established". (أنّ) and its noun; (في الأرض) is the ṣila of (ما); (من شجرة) is in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of [implied] being-settled (istiqrār), or from (ما); and (أقلام) is the predicate of (أنّ).
(وَالْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍ ما نَفِدَتْ كَلِماتُ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): (والبحر): the wāw is circumstantial or conjunctive; (البحر) is mubtadaʾ whose predicate is the clause (يمده), or it is conjoined to the position of (أنّ) and its governed words, since that is nominative as agent, as stated before. (والبحر) has also been read in the accusative, conjoined to the noun of (أنّ). (يمده) [Translator's note: the source prints «وبمده»] is an imperfect verb with a fronted direct object; (من بعده) is a ḥāl; (سبعة أبحر) is the agent of (يمده); the clause (ما نفدت) is the apodosis of (لو), so it has no grammatical position; (إنّ) and its noun; (عزيز) is its first predicate and (حكيم) its second predicate.

* Benefits:
1- We spoke earlier about «لو» and promised you that we would relate the dispute that arose among the grammarians and parsers concerning this verse, about which the debate has been long. We shall present you with a summary of their views so that you may come upon astonishing skill in deduction and precision in logic.
Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn al-Qarāfī said: "The rule of «لو» is that when it enters upon two affirmatives they become negatives, upon two negatives they become affirmatives, and upon a negative and an affirmative the negative becomes affirmative and the affirmative negative. You say: 'Had he come to me, I would have honoured him' — they are two affirmatives, so he did not come to you and you did not honour him. 'Had he not borrowed, he would not have been dunned' — they are two negatives, and he did borrow and was dunned. 'Had he not believed, his blood would have been shed' — the implied meaning is that he believed and his blood was not shed; and conversely: 'Had he believed, he would not have been killed.' Once this rule is established, it would follow that the words of Allah have been exhausted, and that is not so; because «لو» has entered upon an affirmative first and a negative last, so the first becomes negative — and so it is, for the trees are not pens — and it would follow that the last negative becomes affirmative, so that they would be exhausted, and that is not so. The counterpart of this verse is his saying, upon him be blessings and peace: 'What an excellent servant is Ṣuhayb! Had he not feared Allah, he would not have disobeyed Him,' since that entails that he feared and disobeyed despite the fear, which is uglier, and so that would be a sin. But the ḥadīth has been dealt with, and it is the habit of learned men to be very fond of the ḥadīth; as for the verse, few have noticed it. They have mentioned several explanations of the ḥadīth, but as for the verse I have not seen anything from anyone about it; it can be explained along the lines of what they said about the ḥadīth, except that an answer to both the ḥadīth and the verse together has occurred to me, and I shall mention it later.
Ibn ʿUṣfūr said: «لو» in the ḥadīth is in the sense of «إن», for absolute connection, without its negative becoming affirmative or its affirmative negative; so the difficulty is removed. Shaykh Shams al-Dīn al-Khusrawshāhī said: «لو» in the original language is for absolute connection; it became well known in customary usage only for the inversion of its affirmative into negative and vice versa, and the ḥadīth came only with the word's meaning in the language. Shaykh Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām said: a single thing may have a single cause, so that it ceases when that ceases; and it may have two causes, such that its non-existence does not follow from the non-existence of one of them, because the second cause takes the place of the first — as we say of a husband who is a paternal cousin: 'Had he not been a husband, he would have inherited', i.e. as a residuary heir (bi-l-taʿṣīb); for these are two causes, the non-existence of one of which does not entail the non-existence of the other. So too here: people for the most part refrain from disobedience only because of fear, so when fear goes they disobey, the cause being single in their case. So he ﷺ reported that in Ṣuhayb, may Allah be pleased with him, two causes came together preventing him from disobedience — and this is great praise and fine speech. Others answered that the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being 'Had he not feared Allah, Allah would have protected him', and that His saying 'he would not have disobeyed Him' indicates it. These answers can apply to the verse, except the third, for the words of Allah the Exalted not being exhausted, and being without end, is a matter established for them by their very essence, and what is by essence is not explained by causes — so reflect on that. This is the speech of the learned men that has reached me."
Al-Qarāfī continues: "What has occurred to me is that the original use of «لو» is to connect two things, as stated before; then it is also used to cut the connection, so that it is an answer to a real or imagined question in which a connection occurred, and you cut it because you believe that connection to be false. For instance, if someone said 'Had this one not been a husband, he would not have inherited', you say: 'Had he not been a husband, he would not have been deprived [of inheritance]', meaning that the connection you mentioned between the absence of marriage and the absence of inheritance is not correct; your purpose is to cut the connection of his speech, not to connect your own speech. And you say: 'Had Zayd not been learned, he would [still] have been honoured', i.e. for his courage, in answer to a questioner who imagines it, or whom you heard saying that if he were not learned he would not be honoured, connecting the absence of learning with the absence of honour; so you cut that connection. Your purpose is not to connect the absence of learning with honour, for that is not fitting nor among the purposes of rational people; your speech is directed only at the absence of connection. So too the ḥadīth: since what predominates in people is that their disobedience is connected with the absence of the fear of Allah the Exalted, and that this is in people's notions, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut this connection and said: 'Had he not feared Allah, he would [not] disobey Him' [Translator's note: the source reads «لو لم يخف الله يعصه» without «لم» here]. Likewise, since what predominates is that if all the trees became pens and the salt sea along with others [became ink] and everything were written with it, imagination says: nothing could be written with this but would be exhausted, whatever it might be — Allah cut this connection and said: 'they would not be exhausted…' etc. This answer is more fitting than the previous answers for two reasons: first, it covers both these places, while some of them did not cover them, as stated before; second, [taking] «لو» in a sense contrary to the apparent [is a departure], whereas the answer I mentioned does not contradict the usage of the people of the language, for they use what I mentioned and understand nothing else in those instances. And this answer fits well both what is necessary by essence — the attributes of Allah the Exalted and His words — and the contingent that admits of causal explanation, like the obedience of Ṣuhayb, may Allah be pleased with him." End of the words of Shihāb al-Dīn.
As for Ibn Hishām, after mentioning that «لو» is used in five ways, he said: "The second is that it conveys the impossibility (non-occurrence) of both the condition and the apodosis together. This is the view current on the tongues of the parsers, and a group of grammarians stated it explicitly; and it is refuted by many places, among them the saying of Allah the Exalted: «ولو أننا نزلنا إليهم الملائكة وكلمهم الموتى وحشرنا عليهم كل شيء قبلا ما كانوا ليؤمنوا», and «ولو أن ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله», and the saying of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: 'What an excellent servant is Ṣuhayb! Had he not feared Allah, he would not have disobeyed Him.' The explanation is that whenever a thing is impossible, its contradictory is established: if 'he did not stand' is impossible, 'he stood' is established, and vice versa. On this basis, it would follow on this view in the first verse that their belief is established despite the angels not being sent down, the dead not speaking to them and all things not being gathered before them; in the second, that the words are exhausted despite all the trees on earth not being pens writing the words, the greatest sea not being as the inkwell, and the seven seas not being filled with ink and replenishing that sea; and in the report, that disobedience is established despite fear being established. All of that is the opposite of what is intended. The third is that it conveys the impossibility of the condition only, and has no indication of the impossibility of the apodosis nor of its being established. However, if [the apodosis] is equal to the condition in generality, as in your saying 'Had the sun been risen, daytime would have existed', its negation follows, because the negation of the effect follows from the negation of the equal cause; and if it is more general, as in your saying 'Had the sun been risen, light would have existed', its negation does not follow — only the negation of the portion of it equal to the condition follows. This is the view of the verifying scholars (al-muḥaqqiqūn)." — until he says:
"In summary, on this basis it may be said that «لو» indicates three things: the binding of cause and effect, their being in the past, and the impossibility (non-occurrence) of the cause. Then sometimes a fitting connection between the two parts is conceivable, and sometimes it is not. The first kind is of three divisions:
That in which law or reason requires the effecthood of the second to be confined to the causality of the first, such as the saying of Allah the Exalted «ولو شئنا لرفعناه بها», and 'Had the sun been risen, daytime would have existed'. In this, the impossibility of the second follows decisively from the impossibility of the first.
That in which one of them requires the absence of that confinement, such as 'Had he slept, his ablution would have been invalidated'; in this, the impossibility of the second does not follow from the impossibility of the first, as we stated before.
And that in which reason allows it, such as 'Had Zayd come to me, I would have honoured him'; for reason allows the cause of honouring to be confined to the coming, and it is preponderant because that is what appears from the consequence of the second upon the first, it is what springs to mind, and [it accords with] presuming the continuity of the original state. In this kind, reason indicates the negation of the material [Translator's note: so in the source, «المادي»; Mughnī has «المساوي» "equal"] effect because of the negation of the cause, not negation absolutely, while usage and custom indicate absolute negation.
The second kind (that in which no fitting connection between the two parts is conceivable) is of two divisions. One of them is that in which the confirmation of the apodosis is intended, whether the condition exists or not, but with its absence it is more fitting; that is like the report related from ʿUmar about Ṣuhayb, may Allah be pleased with them both: 'What an excellent servant is Ṣuhayb! Had he not feared Allah, he would not have disobeyed Him.' It indicates the confirmation of non-disobedience in every case, and that the negation of disobedience when fear is present is all the more fitting. «لو» did not indicate the negation of the apodosis for two reasons:
First: its indication of that is only by way of mafhūm al-mukhālafa (contrary implication), and in this report mafhūm al-muwāfaqa (congruent implication) indicates the absence of disobedience — because if disobedience is negated when fear is absent, then when fear is present all the more so; and when these two implications conflict, congruent implication takes precedence.
Second: since the fittingness was missing, causality was negated, so the absence of fear was not made the cause of the absence of disobedience. We thus learnt that the absence of disobedience is caused by something else, namely modesty, awe, reverence and veneration, and that continues with fear; so the absence of disobedience in the absence of fear rests on that cause alone, and in the presence of fear rests on it alone or on it and on fear together. On this basis the previous verse of 'Luqmān' is explained, because reason holds decisively that if the words are not exhausted with the abundance of these things, then that they not be exhausted with their scarcity and the absence of some of them is all the more fitting."
Moreover, whoever has attributed the report in these words to the Prophet ﷺ has erred; what has come down is only what Abū Nuʿaym related in al-Ḥilya, that the Prophet said of Sālim, the freedman of Abū Ḥudhayfa, that he was intensely loving towards Allah the Exalted: "Even if he did not fear Allah, he would not disobey Him."
2- Why is "tree" singular?:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it said 'of trees' (min shajaratin) in the singular, rather than the collective noun, which is shajar? I say: what is meant is to go through the trees in detail and exhaustively, tree by tree, so that not a single one of the kind 'tree' remains but has been pared into pens."
He made "tree" singular because, as is established in the science of meanings (ʿilm al-maʿānī), the comprehensiveness of the singular is more inclusive; so it is as though He said: every single tree, so that not one of the kind 'tree' remains but has been pared into pens. And He made "pens" plural to convey multiplicity, i.e. if every tree of the trees were counted as pens.

dervis-irab:28-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كَالظُّلَلِ): al-ẓulal is the plural of ẓulla, with ḍamma on the ẓāʾ: anything that overshadows you, whether a mountain, a cloud, trees or anything else.
(خَتَّارٍ): an intensive form from al-khatr, which is the worst treachery. From it comes their saying: "You do not stretch out to us a span of treachery (ghadr) but we stretch out to you a fathom of perfidy (khatr)." [The poet] said:
وانك لو رأيت أبا عمير ... ملأت يديك من غدر وختر
(If you saw Abū ʿUmayr, you would fill your hands with treachery and perfidy.)
In his saying "you would fill your hands with treachery and perfidy" he likened the abstract to the concrete by way of implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), and "filling the hands" is the imaginative attribution (takhyīl). It is related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man counting on the fingers of his right hand: "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no might nor power except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty", and on the fingers of his left: "O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, provide for me and restore me." So the Messenger of Allah said: "You have filled your hands with good."

* I'rab:
(ما خَلْقُكُمْ وَلا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ): (ما) is negative; (خلقكم) is mubtadaʾ (subject); (ولا بعثكم) is conjoined to (خلقكم); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; the kāf is the khabar (predicate) of (خلق), or the preposition with its genitive noun is the predicate of (خلق). A muḍāf must be supplied, i.e. "except as the creation of a single soul", and "your resurrection is only as the resurrection of a single soul". The speech is resumptive, introduced to answer the doubters who said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah created us in stages — a drop, then a clot, then a lump, then bones — and then you say that we shall be resurrected as a new creation all together in a single hour!" (إنّ) and its noun; (سميع) is its first predicate and (بصير) its second predicate.
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ): the hamza is for the disapproving, affirming question; (لم) is a particle of negation, transformation [of tense] and the jussive; (أنّ) with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of (تر); (أنّ) and its noun; the clause (يولج الليل في النهار) is its predicate, and the clause (يولج النهار في الليل) is conjoined to it.
(وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; (سخر) is conjoined to (يولج) — the reason for the difference in form will come in the section on rhetoric; (الشمس) is the object of (سخر); (القمر) is conjoined to (الشمس); (كل) is mubtadaʾ and the clause (يجري) predicate; (إلى أجل) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يجري) — the secret of this particle will come in the section on rhetoric; (أنّ) and its noun; (بما تعملون) is attached to (خبير); and (خبير) is the predicate of (أنّ).
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّ ما يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ الْباطِلُ): (ذلك) is mubtadaʾ and its predicate is (بأن الله); [the Name] is the noun of (أنّ); (هو) is the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; (الحق) is the predicate of (أنّ), or the predicate of (هو) with the clause being the predicate of (أنّ). (وأنّ) is conjoined to (بأنّ); (أنّ) and its noun; the clause (يدعون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما); (من دونه) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and (الباطل) is the predicate of (أنّ).
(وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ): conjoined to what precedes.
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ الْفُلْكَ تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِنِعْمَتِ اللَّهِ): the hamza is again for the disapproving, affirming question; (لم) is a particle of negation, transformation and the jussive; (تر) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (أنّ) with what follows it is in the position of the accusative as the object of (تر); (أنّ) and its noun; the clause (تجري في البحر) is its predicate; and (بنعمة الله) is a ḥāl, i.e. accompanied by His favour.
(لِيُرِيَكُمْ مِنْ آياتِهِ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ): the lām is causal; (يريكم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām; (من آياته) is in the position of the accusative as the second object of (يريكم). (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is the fronted predicate of (إنّ); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (آيات) is the noun of (إنّ); (لكل) is an adjective of (آيات); (صبار) is annexed to (كل) [as muḍāf ilayhi]; and (شكور) is an adjective of (صبار).
(وَإِذا غَشِيَهُمْ مَوْجٌ كَالظُّلَلِ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (غشيهم) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (غشيهم) is a past verb and a direct object; (موج) is the fāʿil (agent); (كالظلل) is an adjective of (موج); the clause (دعوا الله) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; (مخلصين) is a ḥāl; (له) is attached to (مخلصين); and (الدين) is the object of (مخلصين), because it is an active participle.
(فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ فَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (لما) is the temporal adverbial "when" (ḥīniyya ẓarfiyya) or linking; (نجاهم) is a past verb, a direct object, and a latent agent, its implied form being "He"; (إلى البر) is attached to (نجاهم). The fāʾ is consequential (tafrīʿiyya); (منهم) is a fronted predicate and (مقتصد) a postponed mubtadaʾ, i.e. moderate in disbelief and wrongdoing, because he was restrained to some extent. It has also been said that the muqtaṣid is the one midway between the one who forges ahead in good deeds and the one who wrongs himself. In the speech there is concision (ījāz), which will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَما يَجْحَدُ بِآياتِنا إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارٍ كَفُورٍ): the wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negative; (يجحد) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (بآياتنا) is attached to (يجحد); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (كل) is the agent; (ختار) is muḍāf ilayhi; and (كفور) is an adjective of (ختار).

* Rhetoric:
Difference in verb form and in the two prepositions:
In His saying «وسخر الشمس والقمر» there is a difference of form between the conjoined (سخر) and the (يولج) to which it is conjoined. That is because the insertion of each of the two (night and day) into the other is renewed at every moment, so it is expressed with the form that is renewed time after time; whereas the subjection of the two luminaries is a matter that is neither renewed nor multiplied, but is a continuous, successive permanence, so it is expressed with the past form, [as something] in being.
In His saying «إلى أجل غير مسمى» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى»] there is a difference between the preposition «إلى» used here and the preposition «اللام» used in another place. It is not a case of the two particles interchanging: the first is for termination and the second for specification, and each of them occurs in its proper place, suited to the soundness of the purpose aimed at. For your saying "it runs to (ilā) an appointed term" means it reaches it and ends at it, while your saying "it runs for (li-) an appointed term" means it runs in order to attain an appointed term. What ends here is the utmost point at which creation ends, so the mention of «إلى» was fitting; and what is in [Surat] Fāṭir and al-Zumar is not of this kind, so the mention of the lām was fitting. This is one of the wonderful subtleties, so reflect.
[Translator's note: the I'rab section promised a discussion of the concision (ījāz) in «فمنهم مقتصد» in the section on rhetoric; it does not appear in this entry's rhetoric section.]

dervis-irab:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَاخْشَوْا يَوْماً لا يَجْزِي والِدٌ عَنْ وَلَدِهِ): (اتقوا ربكم) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (واخشوا) is conjoined to (اتقوا); (يوما) is the direct object; and the clause (لا يجزي والد عن ولده) is an adjective of (يوما).
(وَلا مَوْلُودٌ هُوَ جازٍ عَنْ والِدِهِ شَيْئاً إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ): (ولا مولود) is conjoined to (والد); (هو) is mubtadaʾ (subject) and (جاز) khabar (predicate), its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns; the clause is an adjective of (يوما). (شيئا) is the object of (جاز) or of (يجزي), so the question belongs to the topic of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing for one governed word). (إن وعد الله حق): (إنّ), its noun and its predicate.
(فَلا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (implying an omitted condition); (لا) is prohibitive; (تغرنكم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive by the prohibitive (لا); (الحياة) is the agent of (تغرنكم) and the kāf its object; (الدنيا) is an adjective of (الحياة). (ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور) is conjoined to what precedes and parallel to it in its i'rab. Al-gharūr, with fatḥa on the ghayn, is everything that causes one to be deceived and seduced.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ ما فِي الْأَرْحامِ): resumptive speech, introduced to establish Allah's being alone in encompassing the unseen. The occasion of its revelation is that al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥāritha came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about the Hour, when will it come? I have cast my seed [Translator's note: the source reads «حياتي» "my life", evidently for «حَبّي» "my seed/grain"] into the ground, and the sky has been slow [to rain] on us, so when will it rain? And tell me about my wife: she has conceived what is in her womb — is it male or female? I know what I knew yesterday, so what will I do tomorrow? And this is my birthplace, which I know — so where shall I die?"
(إنّ) and its noun; (عنده) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted predicate; (علم الساعة) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is the predicate of (إنّ). (وينزل الغيث) is conjoined to (عنده علم الساعة), so it is in effect a second predicate; and (ويعلم ما في الأرحام) is likewise conjoined.
(وَما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ ماذا تَكْسِبُ غَداً): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (تدري) is an imperfect verb and (نفس) its agent; (ماذا) is a compound interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of (تكسب); the clause (تكسب) stands in place of the two objects of (تدري), which is suspended (muʿallaq) [from governing] by the interrogative; (غدا) is an adverb attached to (تكسب). It is also possible that (ما) is mubtadaʾ and (ذا) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as predicate. The discussion of (ماذا) has preceded.
(وَما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (تدري) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (نفس) is the agent; (بأي أرض) is attached to (تموت), and it suspends the [verb of] knowing, so the clause is in the position of the accusative. The bāʾ is locative, in the sense of (في), i.e. "in which land". (إنّ), its noun and its predicate.

* Rhetoric:
Pronouns have great importance in eloquence and rhetoric, and they affect the strength or weakness of speech, or its being emphatic or not. Among such cases is His saying «ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئا»: the pronoun came after (مولود) and did not come after (والد) in His saying «لا يجزي والد عن ولده شيئا», and that is for a secret that goes beyond i'rab. Imam al-Zamakhsharī gave an answer of the utmost precision, but he overlooked an important matter that tells against it. The following is the text of his words:
"If you say: His saying 'nor will a child be (hū) availing his father anything' comes in an emphatic manner that the clause to which it is conjoined does not — I say: that is so, because the nominal clause is more emphatic than the verbal, and to that are added His saying 'hū' and His saying 'mawlūd' (child). The reason for its coming in this way is that the address is to the believers, and the fathers of most of them died in disbelief and in the religion of the Jāhiliyya; so it was intended to cut off their hopes, and the hopes of people regarding them, that they might benefit their fathers in the Hereafter, intercede for them, and avail them anything against Allah. Therefore it was brought in the most emphatic manner."
It is clear from this beautiful explanation that it applies to those living in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, or that it is specific to them; whereas the correct view is that it is general to them and to everyone to whom the name "people" applies. So it is more fitting to say in answer to the question: since Allah the Exalted emphasised the injunction regarding parents, joined thanks to them with the obligation of thanks to Him, Mighty and Majestic is He, and obliged the child to spare his parent what harms him to the utmost of his ability and the limit of his capacity, He here cut off the parent's notion that the child on the Day of Resurrection would be likely to repay him his due and spare him the terrors of the Resurrection he would meet, just as Allah obliged him to do so for him in this world. And since the child's availing the parent was something whose occurrence might be supposed and a place of hope — because Allah urged him to it in this world — it deserved emphatic negation to remove this notion. This does not apply in the case of the parent towards the child. This is of considerable excellence, so reflect on it.

dervis-irab:1-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ): lahw is every falsehood that distracts from good. One says "lahawtu lahwan", and "so-and-so is occupied with diversions (malāhī)". "And among them is a place of diversion and a playground." Zuhayr said:
وفيهن ملهى للصديق ومنظر ... أنيق لعيّن الناظر المتوسم
(And among them is a diversion for the friend and an elegant sight for the eye of the discerning beholder.) Al-malhā is lahw or the place of it. He says: among these women is a diversion, or a place of diversion, for the one who loves elegance and beauty of appearance, and sights that delight the eye of the beholder who seeks out their charms and marks of beauty.
(وَقْراً): deafness.

* I'rab:
(الم تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْحَكِيمِ هُدىً وَرَحْمَةً لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ) The i'rab of الم has preceded. تلك is the subject, آيات الكتاب the predicate, and الحكيم an adjective of الكتاب; the meaning of attributing wisdom to it will come in the chapter on rhetoric. هدى ورحمة are two ḥāls from الآيات, and the operator in them is the sense of pointing in تلك. Ḥamza read them in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "it is guidance and mercy". للمحسنين is attached to an omitted element as an adjective, or to the maṣdar itself. (الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ) الذين is an adjective of المحسنين, the clause يقيمون الصلاة is the ṣila, and يؤتون الزكاة is conjoined to it, within the scope of the ṣila. هم is the subject, بالآخرة is attached to يوقنون, the second هم is emphasis of the first, and the clause يوقنون is the predicate of هم. (أُولئِكَ عَلى هُدىً مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) This verse preceded in its wording in Sūrat al-Baqara.
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to affirm the state of the idlers who drain their free time with diversion, laughable talk, and idle and false speech. What they said about the occasions of its revelation will come in the chapter on benefits. ومن الناس is a fronted predicate and من is a relative noun, a postponed subject. Min is singular in wording and plural in meaning; its wording was heeded first in three pronouns, يشتري, يضل and يتخذ, and its meaning was heeded in two places, أولئك and لهم, then it returned to the wording in five pronouns, namely وإذا تتلى to the end of the verse, as will come. The clause يشتري لهو الحديث is the ṣila. In ليضل the lām denotes reason, and يضل is an imperfect verb subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām of reason; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يشتري, and عن سبيل الله is attached to يضل. بغير علم is a ḥāl from the agent of يشتري, i.e. "he buys without knowing the state of what he buys". The establishment of the metaphor in "buying" has preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara. (وَيَتَّخِذَها هُزُواً أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ) ويتخذها is in the accusative, conjoined to ليضل; it was also read in the nominative, conjoined to يشتري; and the pronoun refers to السبيل because it is feminine. يتخذها is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "he"; the hāʾ is the first object of يتخذ and هزوا its second object. أولئك is the subject, لهم a fronted predicate, عذاب a postponed subject, مهين an adjective, and the sentence is the predicate of أولئك.
(وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ آياتُنا وَلَّى مُسْتَكْبِراً) The wāw is a conjunction and إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause تتلى is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. تتلى is a passive imperfect verb, عليه is attached to تتلى, and آياتنا is the deputy agent. The clause ولى has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and مستكبرا is a ḥāl. (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْها كَأَنَّ فِي أُذُنَيْهِ وَقْراً فَبَشِّرْهُ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ) كأن is the lightened form of the heavy kaʾanna, its noun the omitted pronoun of the matter, and the clause لم يسمعها is its predicate; the sentence is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of ولى. كأن is a particle of comparison and accusative; في أذنيه is the fronted predicate of kaʾanna, and وقرا its postponed noun [Translator's note: the source says "noun of kāna"; kaʾanna is meant]; the sentence is also a ḥāl from the agent of لم يسمعها, or a badal of the sentence كأن لم يسمعها. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that the two comparison sentences be resumptive. فبشره: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; بشره is an imperative verb with a latent pronoun as agent, its implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is a direct object. The command to give glad tidings is meant sarcastically. بعذاب is attached to بشره, and أليم is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī):
In the words of the Exalted «الكتاب الحكيم» there is a figurative attribution, and it may be in the sense of "possessor of wisdom". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that the original was 'the Book whose Speaker is wise (al-ḥakīm qāʾiluhu)', so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place; with its change to the nominative after the genitive, (the pronoun) became latent in the assimilated adjective afterwards." This is among the most wonderful explanations.
2- Concision (al-ījāz):
In His words «للمحسنين» there is an eloquent concision, i.e. those who do good deeds, which cannot be counted, but He singled out these three. The like of this concision is the saying of Aws ibn Ḥajar in his elegy for Faḍāla ibn Kalada:
الألمعي الذي يظن بك الظن ... كأن قد رأى وقد سمعا
(The keen-minded one, who conjectures about you a conjecture as if he had seen and heard.) It is related of al-Aṣmaʿī that he was asked about the "alma'ī" and recited this to him and added nothing. This elegy is among the best that has been heard in elegy, and its beginning is:
أيتها النفس أجملي جزعا ... إن الذي تحذرين قد وقعا
إن الذي جمع السماحة والنجد ... ة والبر والتقى جمعا
الألمعي الذي يظن إلخ ...
أودى فلا تنفع الاشاحة من ... أمر لمن يحاول البدعا
(O soul, be fair in your grief; what you feared has come to pass. The one who combined generosity, valour, piety and devotion... the keen-minded one who conjectures, etc. He has perished, and being on guard is of no use against a matter for one who seeks novelty.) He says: O soul, bear great grief, for what you fear has occurred, and he made it clear by "the one who combined...". Awdā: he perished; jamaʿā with ḍamma is an emphasis of the attributes before it; and al-alma'ī is accusative as an adjective of "alladhī". He explained that he is the one who conjectures about you, meaning every addressee, i.e. he conjectures the true conjecture, as if he had seen and heard what he conjectured; or he conjectures and hits the mark as if he had seen it, were it an act, or heard it, were it a word. In it is a kind of badīʿ called al-tafsīr, which is to bring a meaning that understanding cannot grasp without its explanation.

* Benefits:
1- The story of al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith:
Know that the intention of the verses of Allah is that the address in them be directed to everyone, but the occasions of revelation are specific, and then their rulings extend afterwards to everyone. They have mentioned, among the occasions of revelation of His words «ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث», that al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith used to come to al-Ḥīra, trade, buy books of the reports of the non-Arabs, and relate them to the people of Mecca, saying: "Muḥammad relates to you the tales of ʿĀd and Thamūd, and I relate to you the tales of Persia and Rome", so they found his talk agreeable and left off listening to the Qur'an. Al-Ḥīra, with kasra on the ḥāʾ, is a city near Kufa.
2- The meaning of the annexation:
The annexation of lahw to ḥadīth has the sense of clarification, which is the annexation in the sense of min; its rule is that the muḍāf following the muḍāf ilayhi be fit to be predicated of it, as in "a ring of silver". This discussion has passed in another place in this book.

dervis-irab:8-11.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ النَّعِيمِ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to explain the state of the believers. inna and its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to آمنوا; لهم is a fronted predicate and جنات النعيم a postponed subject; and the nominal sentence is the predicate of inna. (خالِدِينَ فِيها وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) خالدين is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) from the noun governed by the lām in لهم, i.e. their eternity in it being decreed for them when they enter it; فيها is attached to خالدين. وعد الله and حقا are two emphatic maṣdars: the first emphasises itself and the second emphasises something else, because the meaning of «لهم جنات النعيم» is that Allah promised them it, so He emphasised the meaning of the promise with the promise; and حقا indicates the sense of firmness, with which the sense of the promise was emphasised. Their operators differ: the implied form of the first is "Allah promised that a promise", and of the second "and it is His due, truly"; and the emphasiser of both is one, namely His words «لهم جنات النعيم». هو is the subject, العزيز the first predicate and الحكيم the second predicate. (خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها) The sentence is resumptive, introduced as proof of His power and might, Glory be to Him. خلق is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; السموات is a direct object; بغير عمد is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. a ḥāl of عمد, and its like has passed in al-Raʿd; the clause ترونها is an adjective of عمد, i.e. "without pillars that are seen". (وَأَلْقى فِي الْأَرْضِ رَواسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ وَبَثَّ فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ دابَّةٍ) وألقى is conjoined to خلق, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah; في الأرض is attached to ألقى; رواسي is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "firm mountains"; أن and what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative as an object of purpose, i.e. "lest it shake with you" or "in dislike that it shake with you"; بكم is attached to تميد; وبث is conjoined to ألقى; فيها is attached to بث; and من كل دابة is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "animals of every kind of creature".
(وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ) وأنزلنا is conjoined, by way of a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to the first person; أنزلنا is a verb and agent, من السماء is attached to أنزلنا, and ماء is a direct object. فأنبتنا is conjoined to أنزلنا, فيها is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, and من كل زوج is attached to أنبتنا or is an adjective of an omitted object, i.e. plants of every kind; and كريم is an adjective of زوج. (هذا خَلْقُ اللَّهِ فَأَرُونِي ماذا خَلَقَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِ) هذا is the subject, the pointing being to the creatures mentioned, and خلق الله is the predicate; al-khalq here means the created thing. فأروني: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; أروني is an imperative verb that needs three objects, the yāʾ being the first, and the suspended interrogative sentence stands in place of the remaining two objects. It is also possible that أروني mean "tell me", in which case it takes two objects: the first a plain single word, the pronoun of the speaker, and the second the interrogative sentence. ماذا is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of خلق; or ما is an interrogative noun, a subject, and ذا a relative noun, the predicate. خلق الذين is a verb and agent, and من دونه is the ṣila of الذي. (بَلِ الظَّالِمُونَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) بل is a particle of transitional rejection, الظالمون is the subject, في ضلال the predicate, and مبين an adjective of ضلال.

dervis-irab:12-13.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا لُقْمانَ الْحِكْمَةَ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to show the falsity of polytheism. The lām is the response to an omitted oath, قد is a particle of certainty, آتينا is a verb and agent, لقمان is the first direct object and الحكمة the second direct object. The detailed discussion of Luqmān and his biography will come. (أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ وَمَنْ يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّما يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ) It is possible that أن be the explicative one, because the giving contains the sense of saying, i.e. "We said to him: Give thanks"; and it is possible that it be in its usual function, in which case it is in the interpretation of a maṣdar in the position of the accusative, as Sībawayh related "katabtu ilayhi an qum" (I wrote to him to stand); the first is more evident. لله is attached to اشكر. ومن: the wāw is resumptive, and من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as subject; يشكر is the protasis; the fāʾ links the apodosis; innamā consists of the restrictive and the restricted, and the sentence is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ومن كفر is conjoined to ومن يشكر, within its scope, and the sentence is the predicate of من.
(وَإِذْ قالَ لُقْمانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ) The adverb is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "remember", and the clause قال لقمان is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. لابنه is attached to قال. The wāw is the circumstantial wāw, هو is the subject, and the clause يعظه is the predicate, and the sentence is circumstantial.
(يا بُنَيَّ لا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ) The sentence is the content of the saying. لا is prohibitive, تشرك is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and بالله is attached to تشرك. The sentence إن الشرك gives the reason for the prohibition and has no grammatical position. inna and its noun; the shifted lām; ظلم is its predicate and عظيم an adjective.

* Benefits:
Luqmān, his biography and a glimpse of his reports:
It was said that it is a non-Arabic name, hence diptote because of being a proper name and non-Arabic; it was also said that it is Arabic and a diptote because of being a proper name and having the additional alif and nūn; the first is more evident. The author of al-Qāmūs listed it under the root l-q-m and said: "Luqmān the wise: there is disagreement about his prophethood, and most of the sayings are that he was a sage and was not a prophet."
Because of the charm of his character and the legends woven around it, we give the seven sayings about him in brief:
1- Qatāda said: Allah gave him the choice between prophethood and wisdom, and he chose wisdom, so it was cast upon him while he slept, and he awoke speaking wisdom. He was asked about that and said:
"Had Allah sent prophethood to me as a firm decree, I would have hoped to succeed in it; but He gave me the choice, and I feared that I would be too weak for prophethood."
It was said: he was of the Nubians, short, flat-nosed; it was also said he was Abyssinian.
2- Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: He was a black man from the blacks of Egypt, thick-lipped, and his wisdom was from the wisdom of the prophets. It was said that he was a tailor; it was said a shepherd. A man who knew him before that saw him and said: "Are you not the slave of the Banū so-and-so? Were you not tending sheep yesterday?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what brought you to what I see?" He said: "What astonishes you about my affair?" He said: "People treading on your carpet, crowding at your door, and being content with your word." He said: "Son of my brother, if you do what I tell you, you would be the same." He said: "And what shall I do?" He said: "Lowering my gaze, restraining my tongue, the chastity of my appetite, guarding my private parts, standing by my covenant, fulfilling my promise, honouring my guest, protecting my neighbour, and leaving what does not concern me; that is what made me as you see." It is reported that he said: "The decree of Allah, discharge of trusts, truthfulness in speech, and leaving what does not concern me."
3- Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Wisdom increases the noble in nobility and raises the slave until he sits in the assemblies of kings." Allah the Exalted said: «ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة».
4- The exegete al-Thaʿālibī said: The scholars agreed that Luqmān was not a prophet, except ʿIkrima, who alone held that he was a prophet.
5- Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Luqmān was the son of the sister of Dāwūd, peace be upon him, and it was said the son of his maternal aunt, and he lived in his time. Dāwūd would say to him: "Blessed are you; you were given wisdom and were spared trial", while Dāwūd was given the caliphate and was tried with the trial. Dāwūd would visit him and say: "Look at a man who was given wisdom and protected from temptation."
6- ʿAbd al-Wārith said: Luqmān was given wisdom through a saying he uttered. It was said to him: "Would you like to be a caliph and act with the truth?" He said: "If you choose for me, then hearing and obeying; and if you give me the choice, I choose well-being, for whoever sells the Hereafter for this world loses both; and to live lowly and humble is dearer to me than to live strong and mighty." It was said he was a carpenter slave, and his master said to him: "Slaughter a sheep and bring me the two best morsels." He brought him the heart and the tongue. Then he commanded him likewise, to bring out the two worst morsels, and he brought out the heart and the tongue. He said to him: "What is this?" He said: "There is nothing better than the two when they are good, and nothing worse than the two when they are bad."
7- Abū Isḥāq al-Thaʿlabī said: Luqmān was the least esteemed of his master's slaves in his eyes, so his master sent him with some of his slaves to his orchard to bring some fruit. They came back with nothing, having eaten the fruit and put the blame on Luqmān. Luqmān said to his master: "The two-faced is not honoured with Allah, so give me and them hot water to drink, then send us out to run." He did so, and they began vomiting that fruit while Luqmān vomited water, so his master knew his truthfulness and their lying. It is related that he entered upon Dāwūd, peace be upon him, who was forging a coat of mail; he wished to ask him, but wisdom overtook him and he remained silent. When Dāwūd had finished it, he put it on and said: "What an excellent garment of war you are!" He said: "Silence is wisdom, and few do it." Dāwūd said to him: "You were rightly named the wise."
The reports of Luqmān and his wisdom are too many for a biography to cover, so what has preceded is enough for us.

dervis-irab:14-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَهْناً): al-wahn is weakness. In al-Mukhtār: "al-wahn is weakness; wahana (of the pattern waʿada) and someone else weakened him (wahanahu), being both transitive and intransitive; wahina, with kasra, yahinu wahnan is a dialect of it; awhanahu someone else, and wahhanahu tawhīnan. Al-wahn and al-mawhin are about half the night." Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "It is when the night turns away."
(وَفِصالُهُ): his weaning. In al-Qāmūs: "al-fiṣāl: weaning the child." And in it also: "faṣala the child from nursing, of the pattern ḍaraba."

* I'rab:
(وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَهْناً عَلى وَهْنٍ وَفِصالُهُ فِي عامَيْنِ) A parenthetical sentence by way of digression in the midst of Luqmān's counsel, emphasising the prohibition of polytheism that it contained. ووصينا is a verb and agent, الإنسان is a direct object, and بوالديه is attached to وصينا. The clause حملته أمه is parenthetical between the explained and the explaining. حملته أمه is a past verb, direct object and agent; وهنا على وهن is a ḥāl from أمه, i.e. "possessed of weakness", or an emphatic maṣdar of a verb that is the ḥāl, i.e. "she weakens, weakness"; and على وهن is an adjective of the maṣdar, i.e. "being upon weakness". It was also said it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "she carried him with weakness upon weakness". Al-Zajjāj said: the meaning is that it became incumbent on her, through carrying him, to weaken time after time. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. his mother carried him, she weakening a weakness upon a weakness, as you say 'he returned, return upon the beginning', and it is in the position of a ḥāl; the meaning is that she weakens a weakness above a weakness, i.e. her weakness increases and doubles, because the more the pregnancy grows and gets bigger, the heavier and weaker she becomes." The wāw is a conjunction, فصاله is the subject, and في عامين the predicate.
(أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِي وَلِوالِدَيْكَ إِلَيَّ الْمَصِيرُ) أن is explicative, and the sentence is an explanation of وصينا, as preceded. Al-Zajjāj preferred that أن be in its usual function, i.e. a maṣdar, the position of the maṣdar being the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to وصينا; and his view is not remote. اشكر is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you"; لي is attached to اشكر; ولوالديك is conjoined to لي; إلي is a fronted predicate and المصير the subject; and the sentence is resumptive. (وَإِنْ جاهَداكَ عَلى أَنْ تُشْرِكَ بِي ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلا تُطِعْهُما) The wāw is a conjunction and إن is conditional; جاهداك is a past verb, agent and direct object, and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis; على is a preposition, and the interpreted maṣdar أن تشرك is genitive by على, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to جاهداك; بي is attached to تشرك; ما is a relative, a direct object; the clause ليس is the ṣila; لك is the fronted predicate of ليس; به is attached to علم; and علم is the postponed noun of ليس. فلا: the fāʾ links the apodosis, لا is prohibitive, تطعهما is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, the agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", the hāʾ a direct object, and the mīm and alif two letters indicating the dual; and the sentence فلا تطعهما is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.
(وَصاحِبْهُما فِي الدُّنْيا مَعْرُوفاً) The wāw is a conjunction; صاحبهما is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you", and a direct object; في الدنيا is a ḥāl; معروفا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "an honourable companionship"; and some preferred that it be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with what is right". (وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنابَ إِلَيَّ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) واتبع is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you", سبيل is a direct object, من is a muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause أناب is the ṣila of من; إلي is attached to أناب. ثم is a conjunction of order with delay; إلي is a fronted predicate and مرجعكم a postponed subject. فأنبئكم: the fāʾ is a conjunction, أنبئكم is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "I", and the kāf is a direct object; بما is attached to أنبئكم; كنتم تعملون: kāna and its noun, and the clause تعملون is its predicate.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ما ليس لك به علم» there is the art of inverting the apparent (ʿaks al-ẓāhir), or negating a thing by affirming it, which has been discussed repeatedly. By negating knowledge He intended negating the thing itself, i.e. "do not associate with Me that which is nothing", meaning the idols, in the manner of the saying «على لا حب لا يهتدى بمناره» (on a road with no trail, not guided by its landmark), i.e. that which is not a god, for which you would have knowledge of its divinity.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً﴾: Most readers put "guidance" and "mercy" in the accusative by severance (ʿalā al-qaṭʿ, i.e. as a ḥāl). Ḥamza put them in the nominative as a new beginning (iʾtināf), because it begins anew in a verse separate from the verse before it. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (هُدًى وبُشْرى).

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ﴾: it was revealed about al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith al-Dārī. He used to buy the books of the non-Arabs, Persia and Rome, and the books of the people of al-Ḥīra, (and relate) them to the people of Mecca; and when he heard the Qurʾān he would turn away from it and mock it. That is His saying ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَهَا هُزُواً﴾. The readers differed over ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَهَا﴾: most of them put it in the nominative, and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and his companions put it in the accusative. Whoever reads the nominative refers it back to ﴿يَشْتَرِي﴾, and whoever reads the accusative refers it back to His saying ﴿لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: "and so that he may take it".
His saying ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَهَا﴾ refers to the verses of the Qurʾān. And if you wish, you may make it refer to "the way", because "the way" (al-sabīl) may be feminine; He said ﴿قُلْ هذِهِ سَبِيلِى أَدعُو إِلَي اللهِ﴾, and in the reading of Ubayy: (وإنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الرُشْدِ لاَ يَتّخذُوهَا سَبِيلاً وَإنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الغَىّ يَتّخِذُوهَا سَبِيلاً).
Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us, saying: Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Ḥibbān related to me from Layth from Mujāhid about His saying ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ﴾, he said: it is singing. Al-Farrāʾ said: and the first is its interpretation from Ibn ʿAbbās.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَلْقَىٰ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ﴾: lest it sway with you. (أَنْ) in this position suffices in place of (لا), as the poet said:
* والمهرُ يأبى أن يزال مُلهِبا *
(And the colt refuses to stop running at a blazing pace.)
Its meaning is: refuses not to keep on.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا خَلْقُ ٱللَّهِ﴾: [referring to] what He mentioned of the heavens and the earth, His sending down water from the sky, and His causing [plants] to grow. ﴿فَأَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ﴾ you worship ﴿مِن دُونِهِ﴾, meaning their gods. Then He gave them the lie, saying ﴿بَلِ ٱلظَّالِمُونَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا لُقْمَانَ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us, saying: Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: [145/a] Ḥibbān related to me from someone who related to him, who said: Luqmān was an Abyssinian, with a mutilated nose and thick lips.

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفاً﴾: i.e. keep good company with them.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰبُنَيَّ إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾: "the weight" may be accusative or nominative. Whoever reads the nominative makes it nominative by takun, the indefinite tolerating having no predicate (fiʿl) with kāna, laysa and their sisters. Whoever reads the accusative places in (تكن) an implied, unspecified noun, like the hāʾ in His saying ﴿إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ﴾, and like His saying ﴿فَإنَّهَا لاَ تَعْمَى الأبصارُ﴾. The feminine of (تك) is permissible though "weight" is masculine, because it is annexed to "the grain", and the meaning is about the grain, so the feminine went to it, as he said:
وتشرق بالقول الذى قد أَذَعتَه * كَمَا شَرِقت صَدرُ القناة من الدمِ
(You choke on the word you have spread abroad, as the breast of the spear is choked with blood.)
Had it been ﴿إِن يَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ﴾ it would be correct, and both ways would be permissible in it. His saying ﴿فَتَكُنْ فِي صَخْرَةٍ﴾: it is said that it is the rock beneath the earth, which is Sijjīn, in which the deeds of the disbelievers are written. His saying ﴿يَأْتِ بِهَا ٱللَّهُ﴾: and He will requite for it.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُصَاعِرْ﴾: the people of Medina, ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd and al-Ḥasan read it (تصعِّر) with doubling, and Yaḥyā and his companions read it with the alif: ﴿ولا تُصاعِرْ﴾. He says: do not turn your cheek away from people — from your saying "a man who is aṣʿar (wry-necked)". One may also say "wa-lā tuṣʿir", but I have not heard it.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ أَنكَرَ ٱلأَصْوَاتِ لَصَوْتُ ٱلْحَمِيرِ﴾: he says: the ugliest of voices is the voice of donkeys. You say: "he has an unpleasant (munkar) face" when it is ugly. He said ﴿لَصَوْتُ ٱلْحَمِيرِ﴾; had it been said "the voices of donkeys" it would be correct. But "voice", although attributed to a plural, the plural in this position is like the singular.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظَاهِرَةً وَبَاطِنَةً﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us, saying: Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to me from Khaṣīf al-Jazarī from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read (نِعْمَةً), in the singular. Ibn ʿAbbās said: had it been ﴿نِعَمَهُ﴾, it would be one favour below another favour — or he said: one favour above another favour; the doubt is al-Farrāʾ's. Some people read ﴿نِعَمُه﴾ [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source] as a plural. That is a good reading, because He said ﴿شَاكِراً لأنعُمِه اجْتَباهُ﴾, and this is a plural of favours, which is evidence that ﴿نِعَمَهُ﴾ is permissible.

farraa:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾: the readers read it with the light form, except Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who read it (وَمَنْ يُسَلِّم). It is like your saying to a man: "Commit (aslim) your affair to Allah" and "Hand it over (sallim)".

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلاَمٌ وَٱلْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ﴾: You put ﴿البحر﴾ in the nominative; had you put it in the accusative it would be correct, just as the readers read ﴿وَإذا قِيل إنَّ وَعْدَ اللهِ حَقٌّ والسَّاعَةُ لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهَا﴾ and ﴿الساعة﴾ [i.e. in the accusative]. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍ﴾. He says: it would be ink (midād), like the ink one writes with. ʿAbd Allāh's reading strengthens the nominative. When a thing extends (madda) another thing and increases it, being an increase to it, it "yamudduhu"; you say: "The Tigris feeds (tamuddu) our wells and our rivers", and "Allah supplies us (yumiddunā) with it". You say: "I reinforced you (amdadtuka) with a thousand, and they swelled your numbers (maddūka)". Everything that comes is measured on this.

farraa:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلاَ بَعْثُكُمْ إِلاَّ كَنَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾: except like the raising of a single soul. He left "raising" implied because it is an action, as He said ﴿تَدُورُ أَعْيُنُهُمْ كالذِى يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ (مِنَ المَوْتِ)﴾; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: like the rolling of the eye of one who faints / [145/b] from death; He left both "rolling" and "eye" implied.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿بِنِعْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: it has been read ﴿بنعِمَاتِ الله﴾. The Arabs seldom do that with the pattern fiʿla — make its plural with the tāʾ; they only make its plural on fiʿal, like sidra and sidar (lote trees), khirqa and khiraq (rags). They disliked its plural with the tāʾ only because they oblige themselves to give its second letter kasra when it is pluralised, just as they pluralised ẓulma as ẓulumāt and gave its second letter ḍamma following the ḍamma of its first, and as they said ḥasarāt, making its second follow its first. When they would have been obliged to say bi-niʿimāt, they found it heavy for two kasras to follow one another in their speech, for we have not found that except in ibil (camels) alone. Some of the Arabs have tolerated it and said niʿimāt and sidirāt.

farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿كُلُّ خَتَّارٍ﴾: al-khattār is the treacherous. His saying ﴿مَوْجٌ كالظُلَلِ﴾: He likened it to canopies (ẓulal), while "wave" is singular, because waves ride upon one another and come one thing after another; so He said ﴿كالظُلَل﴾, meaning clouds.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْغَرُورُ﴾: whatever deludes you is gharūr: Satan is gharūr, and this world is gharūr. You say: gharartuhu ghurūran (I deluded him). Had it been read "wa-lā yaghurrannakum bi-llāhi al-ghurūr", meaning the adornment of things, it would be correct.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ ٱلْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلأَرْحَامِ﴾: it carries the interpretation of a negation; the meaning is: no one else knows it. ﴿وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ مَّاذَا تَكْسِبُ غَداً﴾: this came out as a negation; the meaning is overt, and the first is known by the implied negation.
His saying ﴿بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ﴾ and bi-ayyati arḍin: whoever says ﴿بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ﴾ is content with the femininity of "land" and does not show another feminine marker in ayy; whoever uses the feminine says: they have sometimes made do with ayy without what it is annexed to, so the feminine is necessary, as in your saying "I passed by a woman", and you say: "ayyatin (which one)?", and "I passed by two men" [Translator's note: the source has «بجرلين», a slip for «برجلين»], and you say: "ayyayni (which two)?"

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «هُدًى»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الْكِتَابِ}. The preposition «للمحسنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رحمة».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «الذين»: naʿt (adjective) of المحسنين. The clause «هم يوقنون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila (relative clause), and the second «هم» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the first.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The preposition «من ربهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «هدى». «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «ومن الناس من يشتري» is resumptive, and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «مَنْ». The interpreted maṣdar «ليُضِلَّ» is genitive, attached to «يشتري». The preposition «بغير» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يشتري». «هزوا» is a second object. The clause «أولئك لهم عذاب» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items, and the clause «لهم عذاب» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding ṣila (relative clause) {يَشْتَرِي}, with no grammatical position. «مستكبرا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «ولَّى». «كأن» is lightened from the heavy one, and its ism is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لم يسمعها» is the khabar (predicate) of «كأن». The clause «كأن لم يسمعها» is a second ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «ولَّى», and the clause «كأن في أذنيه وقرا» is a third ḥāl from the fāʿil of «ولَّى». The clause «فبشِّره» is conjoined to the clause «ولَّى».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «لهم جنات» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», in the position of the nominative. The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «خالدين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in {لَهُمْ}. The preposition «فيما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خالدين». «وعد»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is omitted, i.e. "Allah promised that, a promising"; it is a maṣdar emphasising itself, because His words {لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ} mean "Allah promised them that". The clause «وَعْدَ» is resumptive. «حقا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governor is omitted, and it is a maṣdar emphasising something else, i.e. the content of the first clause; the implied form is "I affirm that as a truth", and the clause is resumptive. The clause «وهو العزيز» is resumptive, and «الحكيم» is a third khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: the source says "third khabar", although only «العزيز» precedes it in this clause.]

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The preposition «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السموات, and the clause «ترونها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عمد». The interpreted maṣdar «أن تمِيد» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear of". The preposition «من كل» is attached to «أنبتنا».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «فأروني» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «هذا خلق». «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا»: a relative noun, khabar (predicate). The clause «ماذا خلق» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb «أروني». The clause «بل الظالمون في ضلال» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explicative, because it is preceded by something having the meaning of "saying" but not its letters. «من»: a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the linking pronoun in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied, i.e. "of him".

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The wāw is resumptive. «إذ» is the object of an implied (muqaddar) "اذكر" (remember), and the clause «وهو يعظه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). His words «يا بُني»: one addressed in the vocative, a muḍāf, accusative; the sign of its accusative is the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, and the second yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «ووصَّينا» is resumptive, and the clause «حملته أمه» is parenthetical. The clause «وفصاله في عامين» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «حملته». «وهنا» is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أمه». The preposition «على وهن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «وهنا». «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause «اشكر لي» explains the enjoining. The clause «إليَّ المصير» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «وصَّيْنَا». The interpreted maṣdar «أن تشرك» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جاهداك». «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The preposition «لك» is attached to the khabar (predicate), and the preposition «به» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «علم». His words «معروفًا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its adjective standing in for it, i.e. "a kindly companionship". «ثم» in His words «ثم إليَّ» is a particle of resumption, and the clause is resumptive. The clause «فأنبئكم» is conjoined to the clause «إليَّ مرجعكم».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «يا بني» is resumptive, within the scope of the speech. The clause «إنها» with its khabar (predicate) is the response to the vocative, and the conditional clause with its apodosis is the khabar of «إنَّ». «تك»: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with the sukūn implied on the nūn, which was omitted for lightening. The hāʾ in «إنها» is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), and the ism of «تك» is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to the good deed or the evil deed understood from the context. The preposition «من خردل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «حبة». The preposition «في صخرة» is attached to the khabar of «تكن», and the clause «فتكن في صخرة» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «تك مثقال».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «يا بني» is resumptive, within the scope of the speech, and the clause «أقم» is the response to the vocative, resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The preposition «للناس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تُصَعِّر». «مرحا» is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The verb «اقصد» is intransitive, meaning اقتصد (be moderate). «مِنْ» in «مِنْ صوتِك» is partitive (tabʿīḍiyya). «صوت» in His words «لصوت» was put in the singular because the genus is meant by it.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The interpreted maṣdar formed from «أَنّ» and what follows it stands in place of the object of «تروا». «ظاهرة»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نعمه». The clause «ومن الناس» is resumptive. The preposition «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يجادل», and the preposition «في الله» is attached to «يجادل».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila (relative clause) {يُجَادِلُ}. The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «قيل» is the pronoun of the maṣdar. The content of speech after «قالوا» is implied, i.e. "we do not follow what Allah has sent down; rather we follow…". His words «أولو كان»: the hamza is for interrogation, the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «لو» is a non-jussive conditional particle. This wāw conjoins to an implied ḥāl (circumstantial) for comprehensiveness, i.e. "do they follow him in every state, even if Satan were calling them?" The clause «ولو كان» is a ḥāl from the wāw in «يتبعونه», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "they would follow him".

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «ومن يُسْلم» is resumptive, and «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «وهو محسن» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The preposition «إلى الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. The clause «وإلى الله عاقبة الأمور» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «إلينا مرجعهم» is resumptive, and the clause «فننبِّئهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إلينا مرجعهم».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «نمتعهم» is resumptive. «قليلا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «ولئن سألتهم» is resumptive. «مَنْ»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). «الله»: fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e. "Allah created them". The clause «مَنْ خلق» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. His words «ليقولُن»: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and the implied oath clause is resumptive. The verb is an imperfect, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which was omitted because of the succession of similar letters, and the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the fāʿil.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «لله ما في السماوات» is resumptive. The preposition «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «ولو أن ...» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ}. «أنَّ» and what follows it are equivalent to a maṣdar, the fāʿil (agent) of «ثبت». The preposition «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause), and the preposition «من شجرة» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما». «أقلام»: khabar (predicate) of أن. The clause «والبحر يمده» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «ثبت». The preposition «من بعده» is attached to a ḥāl from «سبعة أبحر», and «سبعة» is the fāʿil. The clause «ما نفدت كلمات» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The preposition «كنفس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and the clause «إن الله سميع» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of «ترَ». The clause «كل يجري» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الشمس والقمر». The second interpreted maṣdar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first maṣdar. The preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خبير».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The interpreted maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «ذلك». «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position. The second interpreted maṣdar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first. The second «هو» is a pronoun of separation, and «الكبير» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the object of the seeing. The preposition «بنعمة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تجري», and the genitive maṣdar «ليريكم» is attached to «تجري».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive {أَلَمْ تَرَ}, and the second conditional clause «فلمَّا نجَّاهم» is conjoined to the first conditional clause. The apodosis (jawāb) of «لمَّا» is implied, i.e. "they divided into two groups". The clause «فمنهم مقتصد» is conjoined to the apodosis. The clause «وما يجحد إلا كل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «لا يجزي والد» is a naʿt (adjective) of «يوما», and the linking pronoun is implied, i.e. "in it". His words «ولا مولود»: mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because the negation precedes it. «هو» is a second mubtadaʾ, and «جازٍ» is the khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ, nominative with the ḍamma implied on the omitted yāʾ. The preposition «عن والده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جازٍ». «شيئا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a little or much recompense". The clause «ولا مولود هو جاز» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا يجزي والد», and the linking pronoun is implied, i.e. "in it"; the clause «هو جاز» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «مولود». The clause «إن وعد الله حق» is resumptive, within the scope of the vocative, and the clause «لا تغرنَّكم الحياة» is conjoined to the resumptive «إن وعد الله حق».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The clause «عنده علم الساعة» is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and the clause «وينزل الغيث» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «عنده علم». The clause «ماذا تكسب» is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of «تدري». His words «ماذا»: «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» is a relative noun, khabar. The clause «بأيِّ أرض تموت» stands in place of the two objects of «تدري». The clause «وما تدري نفس» is conjoined to the clause «إن الله عنده».

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying, exalted is He, {هدى وَرَحْمَة}: two aḥwāl (circumstantial expressions) from تلك. It is not good for them to be a ḥāl from الكتاب, because it is a muḍāf ilayhi, so there is no governor to govern the ḥāl, since the possessor of the ḥāl has no governor; there is disagreement about this. Whoever reads ورحمةٌ in the nominative makes هدى in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is guidance and mercy". It may also be the khabar (predicate) of {تِلْكَ}, with {آيَات} as a badal (substitute) for تلك.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {ويتخذها}: whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to ليضل; whoever reads it in the nominative conjoins it to {يَشْتَرِي}, or (reads it) as a break (qaṭʿ, a new start). The hāʾ in يتخذها refers to الآيات.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {بِغَيْر عمد ترونها}: ترونها is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of عمد; so it is possible that there are pillars but they are not seen. It may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السموات, in which case there are no pillars there at all. It may also be in the position of the nominative as a break (qaṭʿ), and then too there are no pillars there.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {مَاذَا خلق الَّذين من دونه}: ما is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is ذا, which has the meaning of الذي; its implied form is "so show me: what thing is it that those besides Him have created?", and the clause is in the position of the accusative by أروني. It is also permissible for ما to be in the position of the accusative by خلق, being interrogative, and you make ذا redundant (zāʾida). It is also permissible for ما to have the meaning of الذي, in the position of the accusative by أروني, with ذا redundant, and you imply the hāʾ with خلق, referring to الذي, i.e. "so show me the things which those besides Him have created".
